entries.argumentHint: [handler | endpoint | file:function | empty to trace the write path in the current diff]

entries.name: mode-contract-first
entries.description: Before any data code or design, prints a data contract card answering the five basic questions, marks unanswered ones OPEN, and does not decide correctness-critical OPEN items silently.

entries.name: mode-failure-first
entries.description: After proposing any change that writes data, handles messages, keeps a copy or changes a contract, shows a failure walk of scenarios, outcomes and guards before the code.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the data-system rule behind each decision, names the trade-off, and ends non-trivial answers with one check-for-understanding question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps and asks before any change larger than a few lines or one that touches a data contract: schema, message shape, public API, partition key or isolation setting.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against the data-intensive rules, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly when clean.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Gives the result first in a few lines with no preamble, adds a one-line data-contract note only when a gap exists, and still shows failing output in full.

entries.name: batch-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of batch jobs: rerun safety, input versioning, atomic output publication, side effects inside replayable steps and partial-failure behavior. Use proactively after edits to ETL, scheduled reports, backfills or reprocessing jobs.

entries.name: capacity-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of performance and scalability claims: load parameters, percentile latency, named bottleneck, evidence and operability of new components. Use when a change or design claims to scale, adds nodes, caches or shards, or reports a speedup.

entries.name: consistency-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the consistency contract: freshness needs per read path, read-your-writes expectations, staleness tolerance and conflict handling for concurrent updates. Use proactively after edits that route reads to replicas, caches or projections, or allow concurrent edits of one record.

entries.name: data-test-writer
entries.description: Implementer of tests only: writes duplicate-delivery, out-of-order, replay, conflict, schema-compatibility and rebuild tests for existing data-path behavior. Use when data-intensive-apps-test-gap-reviewer reports missing tests. Never edits production code.

entries.name: derived-view-builder
entries.description: Implementer that makes one cache, index, projection or read model rebuildable, with a checkpoint, a lag metric and a rebuild entry point. Use when data-intensive-apps-ownership-reviewer or ownership-map flagged a derived copy with no rebuild path, no lag visibility or an inline best-effort write.

entries.name: evolution-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of contract changes: schema, column, API, message, enum and encoding changes against old readers, old writers, stored data and in-flight messages. Use proactively after edits to migrations, schema files, serializers, DTOs or enums.

entries.name: fault-model-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of fault assumptions: timeouts, wall-clock use, locks, leases, leader election, majorities, coordination services and linearizability claims. Use proactively after edits that add a lock, lease, timeout policy, timestamp comparison or leader logic.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the ten-item data-intensive checklist against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence per item. Use before declaring a data-path change done, committing, or opening a pull request.

entries.name: idempotency-hardener
entries.description: Implementer that makes one retry-unsafe handler, consumer or job safe to run twice, with a dedup key or idempotent transition and its duplicate-delivery test. Use when data-intensive-apps-idempotency-reviewer or a replay drill found a duplicate-effect finding in a defined scope.

entries.name: idempotency-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of handlers that can run more than once: consumers, jobs, webhooks, retried commands. Reports effects, dedup mechanism and the result of duplicate delivery and replay. Use proactively after edits to anything fed by a queue, stream, scheduler or retry loop.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for data-intensive work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review that touches storage, messaging, replication, schemas or transactions, to decide which specialists and skills apply, in at most five steps. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: ordering-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of ordering assumptions: what order the logic needs, the scope the transport provides, consumer concurrency per key and version or sequence handling. Use proactively after edits to event consumers, projections or state machines fed by messages.

entries.name: ownership-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of data ownership and derived copies: primary owner, other writers, caches, indexes and projections, propagation, lag visibility and rebuild path. Use proactively after edits that add or write a cache, search index, read model or duplicated field.

entries.name: partitioning-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of partition and routing keys: whether common operations stay on one partition, hot-key and skew risk, cross-partition cost, secondary-index placement and rebalancing. Use when a change adds or alters a shard key, topic key, cache cluster key or fan-out query.

entries.name: replication-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of replication design: leader-follower, multi-leader or leaderless choice, sync versus async, failover behavior, quorum claims, read routing and replica conflict resolution. Use when a change adds or alters replicas, failover, routing to followers or merge logic.

entries.name: schema-migrator
entries.description: Implementer that carries out one contract change (rename, retype, split, enum or format change) as staged expand, migrate and contract steps with compatibility tests. Use when data-intensive-apps-evolution-reviewer or compat-matrix found a breaking change that must ship across releases.

entries.name: service-boundary-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of service boundaries and cross-service contracts: data ownership per service, chatty hot-path calls, split invariants and contract identifiers, versions and failure semantics. Use when a change adds a service, an endpoint between services or a cross-service call.

entries.name: storage-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of data model, index and storage-layout fit: relational versus document versus graph, indexes versus write cost, OLTP versus analytical load, application-side joins, memory residency. Use proactively after edits adding indexes, tables, queries or a new store.

entries.name: stream-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of stream processors and event contracts: event, processing and ingestion time, windows, lateness, state and checkpoints, delivery guarantees, change data capture and event definitions. Use proactively after edits to stream jobs, CDC, event producers or log-fed projections.

entries.name: test-gap-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of tests for data paths: finds missing duplicate, out-of-order, replay, conflict, compatibility and rebuild tests for the behavior a change adds. Use proactively after edits to consumers, jobs, projections, migrations or concurrency guards, and before data-intensive-apps-data-test-writer.

entries.name: transaction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of atomicity scope, isolation and multi-store writes: invariants versus anomalies (lost update, write skew, phantom), dual writes and effects around a commit. Use proactively after edits with check-then-write, transactions, locks, outbox code or multi-store writes. What the caller is told is data-intensive-apps-write-path-reviewer.

entries.name: write-path-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of write paths: what is durable and visible after each step, what a crash or timeout leaves behind, and what the caller is told. Use proactively after edits to handlers or jobs that write a store and then publish, cache, index or call out. Atomicity and anomalies are data-intensive-apps-transaction-reviewer.

entries.name: aggregates
entries.description: Use when deciding what must be consistent together, when a transaction changes several domain objects, when callers mutate a collection inside an object, or when an object holds a live reference to another root. For one object use ddd-entities; for layout ddd-modules-and-associations.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for Domain-Driven Design health and return ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: bounded-contexts
entries.description: Use when deciding where a model starts and stops, when one word means different things in different modules, or when domain types are shared by several contexts. Who owns a model; how two contexts relate: ddd-context-relationships; folder layout: ddd-modules-and-associations.

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the Domain-Driven Design review checklist against the current work, answer yes, no or not applicable with evidence, and give a next step for each no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: choose-structure
entries.description: Decide whether a large model needs a guiding large-scale structure and which, with governance and a review trigger, using the rule set's restraint: minimal, evolving, domain-specific.
entries.argumentHint: [area or system to structure | proposed structure to evaluate | empty to assess the repository root]

entries.name: context-relationships
entries.description: Use when integrating with another team's model, a legacy system or a vendor API, choosing among Shared Kernel, Customer/Supplier, Conformist or Anticorruption Layer, or phasing out a legacy system. The edge between models; for one context's inside use ddd-bounded-contexts.

entries.name: deep-models
entries.description: Use when a model feels shallow, table-shaped or contradictory, when requirements keep adding special cases, or when one concept could simplify many rules. Whole-model judgment and breakthrough refactoring; for a single hidden flag or condition use ddd-explicit-concepts.

entries.name: distillation
entries.description: Use when deciding where modeling effort belongs, when generic mechanisms outweigh and hide the distinctive logic, or when picking refactoring targets by strategic value. Finding the core; types shared across contexts: ddd-bounded-contexts; refusing ceremony in one change: ddd-right-sizing.

entries.name: domain-services
entries.description: Use when a domain operation fits no single entity or value object, when a *Service class collects unrelated rules, or when behavior is moved out of entities only to keep them thin. Services that hold domain decisions; for application orchestration use ddd-layers.

entries.name: domain-tests
entries.description: Use when writing, reviewing or ordering tests for domain behavior: invariants, allowed and forbidden transitions, invalid construction, specifications, application orchestration, and translations at context boundaries. Tests of the model; infrastructure tests stay separate.

entries.name: entities
entries.description: Use when an object has identity and a lifecycle, when setters or public fields let callers edit state, or when it lacks methods for its valid transitions. The entity class itself; for rules in controllers or jobs use ddd-layers, for values ddd-value-objects, for cross-object rules ddd-aggregates.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Domain-Driven Design rule, pattern or section: its strength, the reason, how to check it, an original example and when it bends.
entries.argumentHint: [rule, pattern or section name, for example aggregates or anticorruption layer]

entries.name: explicit-concepts
entries.description: Use when a flag, status string, repeated condition over several values, rule in a comment or script-like process hides a business concept, or a named rule (specification, policy) is needed. Whole model: ddd-deep-models. One value's validation: ddd-value-objects. Rule shape: ddd-supple-design.

entries.name: factories
entries.description: Use when creating a domain object takes several collaborating values or business rules, when endpoints or mappers assemble objects field by field, or when invalid or partly built objects can exist. Creation of new objects; for loading stored ones use ddd-repositories.

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve named Domain-Driven Design findings with the smallest change each, in the rule set's refactoring order, running the tests and never committing.
entries.argumentHint: [findings text | review output | finding numbers | empty to use findings from this session]

entries.name: infrastructure
entries.description: Use when ORM annotations, table shapes, serializers or framework types appear in domain classes, or domain classes take names from tables or columns. Own technical shapes; word choice: ddd-ubiquitous-language; repository contract: ddd-repositories; foreign models: ddd-context-relationships.

entries.name: language-audit
entries.description: Build a concept-to-term table for each context of a tree and find synonyms, overloaded terms, technical stand-ins and doc drift, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: layers
entries.description: Use when controllers, handlers, jobs or application services decide business outcomes, or when choosing a rich domain layer or Smart UI. Which layer decides; ORM shapes in the model: ddd-infrastructure; an entity's setters and transitions: ddd-entities; whether modeling is earned: ddd-right-sizing.

entries.name: map-contexts
entries.description: Reconstruct the context map of a repository as found: contexts, relationships, translation points and leaks, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: model-driven-design
entries.description: Use when design documents, diagrams, tickets and code describe different models, when a model exists only on a whiteboard, or when tests and docs should explain the domain. Alignment of model, code and artifacts; for word choice use ddd-ubiquitous-language.

entries.name: modules-and-associations
entries.description: Use when organizing packages or directories, adding a field that references another domain object, or finding models, services, utils or helpers folders dominating the layout. Folder layout only; shared types: ddd-bounded-contexts; consistency: ddd-aggregates; hidden core: ddd-distillation.

entries.name: pattern-fit
entries.description: Decide whether an analysis pattern, design pattern or industry formalism fits the model without displacing domain names, and report adopt, adapt or reject with a term mapping.
entries.argumentHint: [pattern or formalism name | the concept you want to model | empty to review patterns in the current diff]

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a feature or model change in the rule set's code-generation order: domain concept first, then model, boundaries, translation, tests and steps.
entries.argumentHint: [feature or change description | issue text | empty to plan from the current diff]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Domain-Driven Design rule set (Evans) to design and code decisions. Use for any task that models a business domain, reviews domain code, names things in the language of the business, or integrates with another model, system or team.

entries.name: repositories
entries.description: Use when adding or reviewing a repository: one per table, generic CRUD or query-builder interfaces, persistence records returned instead of domain objects, rules in repository code. The access contract; for new objects use ddd-factories, for ORM or table shapes in domain classes ddd-infrastructure.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Domain-Driven Design rules and report ranked findings with proposed refactorings.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: right-sizing
entries.description: Use when a change adds repositories, factories, aggregates or services to simple CRUD, when DDD vocabulary is applied without a model change, or when deciding how much modeling an area deserves. Brake on ceremony; for the core use ddd-distillation, for which layer decides ddd-layers.

entries.name: scenario-walkthrough
entries.description: Walk a real business scenario through the model and code and report where it turns procedural, awkward or leaky, with the model pressure it reveals.
entries.argumentHint: [scenario in one or two sentences | ticket text | empty to derive one from the current diff]

entries.name: smell-hunt
entries.description: Walk the forbidden-pattern families over a scope and map every hit to a treatment skill and an order of treatment.
entries.argumentHint: [family | all] [path]   families: passive-model, smart-ui, persistence-driven, primitive-obsession, shared-model, god-service, invalid-construction, fake-ddd, context-blindness, pattern-obscurity

entries.name: supple-design
entries.description: Use when a domain API hides intent behind technical names, a method both answers and changes state, invariants live only in comments or UI checks, or named rules are combined. Vocabulary: ddd-ubiquitous-language. Creating a rule: ddd-explicit-concepts.

entries.name: ubiquitous-language
entries.description: Use when naming or renaming domain types, methods, tests or modules, or when synonyms or one word with two meanings inside one context appear. One term per concept; names copied from tables or columns: ddd-infrastructure; stale docs and diagrams: ddd-model-driven-design.

entries.name: value-objects
entries.description: Use when raw strings, numbers or dates stand for money, ranges, codes or measurements, when one value's validation repeats across handlers, or when a descriptive concept is mutable. Attribute-only concepts; for identity use ddd-entities, for a rule over several values ddd-explicit-concepts.

entries.name: mode-context-first
entries.description: Opens every implementation answer with a domain frame: bounded context, domain terms, the kind of model element, and the invariants at stake, before any code.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Domain-Driven Design rule behind each decision, names its strength, and ends non-trivial answers with one question that checks understanding.

entries.name: mode-model-explorer
entries.description: Runs a discovery conversation about the model: asks domain questions, offers two or three candidate model shapes, walks a scenario through each, and writes no code until a shape is chosen.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps as a pair partner for domain-model changes, and asks before any change larger than a few lines or one that touches public API.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Reviews only: every answer is a ranked findings table against the Domain-Driven Design rules, with no rewrites unless asked and an explicit statement when nothing is found.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first and brief: no preamble, a few lines unless more is asked, domain terms named, failing output still shown in full.

entries.name: aggregate-reshaper
entries.description: Implementer that redraws one aggregate boundary: root-only mutation, encapsulated members, references to other aggregates by identity and a smaller transaction scope. Use when review findings report root bypass, live cross-root references or convenience transactions.

entries.name: aggregate-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of aggregate boundaries and transaction scope. Use proactively after edits that change a root and its members, expose internal collections, hold references between roots, or save several domain objects in one transaction.

entries.name: behavior-mover
entries.description: Implementer that moves business rules out of controllers, jobs, application services and repositories into the entity, value object or domain service that owns them. Use when review findings report passive entities or rules in the wrong layer.

entries.name: ceremony-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of DDD ceremony. Use proactively after edits that add repositories, factories, aggregates, domain services, layers, pattern-named types or imported patterns to simple code, to separate real modeling from fake DDD.

entries.name: concept-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of hidden domain concepts. Use proactively after edits that add flags, status or type strings, repeated conditions, magic thresholds, rules in comments or script-like processes, to find the policy, specification or process that should be named.

entries.name: context-boundary-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of bounded contexts and integrations. Use proactively after edits that call another service, consume a vendor or legacy API, or share or reuse domain types across areas, to check ownership, relationships and translation.

entries.name: domain-test-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of tests of the domain model. Use proactively after edits to invariants, transitions, creation rules, specifications, application orchestration or context translation, or after tests are added to check they read in domain language.

entries.name: domain-test-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests of the domain model in the ubiquitous language: invariants, allowed and forbidden transitions, invalid construction and translations. Use when review findings report missing tests, or before a behavior-preserving move. Writes tests only.

entries.name: entity-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of entity classes: identity, setters, public fields, missing transition methods. Use proactively after edits that add or change classes with identity or lifecycle. Rules sitting in controllers, jobs or application services belong to ddd-layer-reviewer.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Domain-Driven Design review checklist against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence per item. Use before declaring work done, committing, or opening a pull request.

entries.name: infrastructure-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of technical shapes inside the domain model. Use proactively after edits that add ORM annotations, table-shaped classes, serializer or framework types, DTO reuse, or persistence-only methods to domain classes.

entries.name: language-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the ubiquitous language in code, tests and documents. Use proactively after edits that add or rename domain types, methods, tests or modules, or when synonyms or overloaded words appear. Names copied from tables or columns go to ddd-infrastructure-reviewer.

entries.name: layer-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of where business decisions live. Use proactively after edits to controllers, handlers, jobs, scripts or application services, or when a Smart UI is proposed, to find rules outside the domain layer and application services that own invariants. The entity class's own surface is ddd-entity-reviewer.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Domain-Driven Design work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review to decide which reviewers, implementers and skills apply, in what order, in at most five steps, and how much modeling the area earns. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: lifecycle-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how domain objects are created and retrieved. Use proactively after edits that add constructors, builders, factories, repositories or data-access interfaces, or let controllers assemble aggregates field by field.

entries.name: module-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of package structure and associations. Use proactively after edits that add packages or directories in a domain area, move files, add references between domain objects, or introduce models, services, utils or helpers folders. Folder layout only.

entries.name: service-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of behavior placement among entities, value objects and domain services. Use proactively after edits that add or grow a *Service, Manager or Handler class holding domain rules, or that move logic out of entities.

entries.name: strategy-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of strategic design choices. Use proactively when a plan or diff affects where modeling effort goes, lets generic mechanisms bury or outweigh the core domain, or changes a context map or large-scale structure without a recorded decision.

entries.name: supple-design-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the model's interface: intention-revealing operations, command and query separation, explicit assertions, conceptual contours and readable rule combination. Use proactively after edits that add or change public domain operations.

entries.name: translation-builder
entries.description: Implementer that builds a translation layer at one boundary: a mapper or anticorruption layer from a foreign or legacy model to the local model, with boundary tests. Use when review findings report foreign terms, vendor codes or transport types leaking into the core.

entries.name: value-object-introducer
entries.description: Implementer that replaces primitive groups and repeated validation with value objects in small, test-backed steps. Use when review findings or a plan call for introducing value types for amounts, ranges, codes, measurements or identifiers.

entries.name: value-object-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of value objects and primitive obsession. Use proactively after edits that add raw strings, numbers or dates for amounts, ranges, codes or identifiers, repeat a validation, or add mutable small data classes.

entries.name: accelerated-modeling
entries.description: Use when workflow, events, commands, policies or team language are unclear, when modeling risks turning into detached analysis, or when delivery pressure tempts skipping design. Covers event storming, timeboxes, spikes, scenarios and expert involvement. Procedure: ddd-distilled-event-storm.

entries.name: adoption-fit
entries.description: Use when deciding whether an area of business software deserves DDD modeling at all, how much effort it earns, or whether an earlier decision needs reassessing. Not for one concept's pattern (ddd-distilled-pattern-economy) or ranking areas (ddd-distilled-subdomains).

entries.name: aggregates
entries.description: Use when deciding what belongs in one aggregate, reviewing its size, root access or references, or when an object graph is loaded and changed as a whole. A request changing several aggregates: ddd-distilled-cross-aggregate-consistency; whether an aggregate is needed: ddd-distilled-pattern-economy.

entries.name: application-services
entries.description: Use when a service, handler or controller makes business decisions, when an application service is shaped by HTTP or message formats, or when deciding what a use-case method may contain. Keeps it to coordination. For logic that moves out see ddd-distilled-entities.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for Domain-Driven Design Distilled health and return ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: bounded-contexts
entries.description: Use when one class or model is shared across billing, identity, catalog, fulfillment or support, when the same word has different rules in different modules, or when module layout ignores context boundaries. Inside one context; for links between two use ddd-distilled-context-mapping.

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the Domain-Driven Design Distilled final checklist against your current work, answering yes, no or not applicable with evidence and a next action for every no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: classify-subdomains
entries.description: Inventory the business capabilities of a codebase, propose core, supporting or generic classes with evidence, flag mismatches between class and modeling effort, and list the questions the user must answer. At most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | product or area description | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: context-mapping
entries.description: Use when two contexts or systems must integrate and the relationship (Partnership, Shared Kernel, Customer/Supplier, Conformist, Anticorruption Layer, Open Host Service, Published Language, Separate Ways) is unstated or wrongly named. Not for translator code (ddd-distilled-context-translation).

entries.name: context-translation
entries.description: Use when another team's model, API payload, event, schema or legacy status codes enter local code, or when an 'anticorruption layer' may translate nothing. Covers translators and their tests. For framework, ORM or HTTP types use ddd-distilled-infrastructure-isolation.

entries.name: cross-aggregate-consistency
entries.description: Use when one request or transaction loads or saves more than one aggregate root, when convenience builds a graph, or when a second aggregate must follow the first. Covers transaction scope, eventual consistency. Event design: ddd-distilled-domain-events; one aggregate: ddd-distilled-aggregates.

entries.name: domain-events
entries.description: Use when naming, designing or reviewing domain events, when events are vague, command-like or fired for every field change, or when deciding whether a fact deserves an event. Delivery: ddd-distilled-integration-styles; transaction scope around events: ddd-distilled-cross-aggregate-consistency.

entries.name: domain-tests
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing tests of domain code: value objects, entity and aggregate transitions, application service orchestration, translators. Tests should read in the ubiquitous language. To build a translator itself use ddd-distilled-context-translation.

entries.name: entities
entries.description: Use when a class has identity and a lifecycle, when public setters let any code change business state, or when an entity is only getters and setters. Covers identity and guarded transitions. Identity-less values: ddd-distilled-value-objects; pattern undecided: ddd-distilled-pattern-economy.

entries.name: estimate-work
entries.description: Size DDD work by modeling uncertainty, integration risk and implementation cost, with team skill and domain-expert access as limits, and say which spike would reduce the uncertainty most.
entries.argumentHint: [feature list | epic text | path to a plan | empty to ask]

entries.name: event-storm
entries.description: Run a timeboxed, text-based event storming session with the user for one business process and end with a timeline, glossary entries, candidate boundaries, scenarios and a spike list.
entries.argumentHint: [process or workflow to explore | path to notes | empty to ask]

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Domain-Driven Design Distilled rule: its strength, the reason behind it, how to check it in code, an original example and the exception the book allows.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | section heading | question about a rule | empty to list the sections]

entries.name: explicit-concepts
entries.description: Use when a boolean, status code, enum, flag, magic string or helper method carries a business decision, or code could belong to any business. Promotes hidden concepts to named ones. For repeated data values use ddd-distilled-value-objects; for names alone, ddd-distilled-ubiquitous-language.

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given Domain-Driven Design Distilled findings with the smallest change per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Stops at modeling decisions. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: glossary
entries.description: Build a per-context table of domain terms from a codebase, and report synonyms, homonyms and placeholder names with the files that show them. At most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | context name | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: infrastructure-isolation
entries.description: Use when framework, ORM, persistence, REST or JSON types appear in domain code, when tables or API schemas drive the model, or when a domain method needs a request, session or serializer. For another team's model use ddd-distilled-context-translation.

entries.name: integration-styles
entries.description: Use when choosing or reviewing how contexts talk: RPC, REST resources or asynchronous messaging, and whether a domain event carries its data or makes consumers query back. For converting the foreign model use ddd-distilled-context-translation.

entries.name: map-contexts
entries.description: Reconstruct the as-found context map of a codebase: contexts, integration edges, the relationship each edge shows in practice versus what it is called, and dishonest claims. Whole tree, not a diff: to judge a change use ddd-distilled-relationship-reviewer or ddd-distilled-context-boundary-reviewer. At most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: model-first
entries.description: Produce a short model brief before writing new domain behavior: capability, subdomain, context, local terms, concept kinds, smallest patterns, boundaries and scenarios, following the Domain-Driven Design Distilled generation order.
entries.argumentHint: [feature or behavior to build | empty to ask]

entries.name: modeling-debt
entries.description: Record a deliberately deferred modeling imperfection with where it is, why it was deferred, what carrying it costs and what triggers repayment; or review an existing register for items whose trigger has fired.
entries.argumentHint: [what was deferred | 'review' + path to a register | empty to ask]

entries.name: pattern-economy
entries.description: Use when deciding which pattern a concept needs (record, value object, entity, aggregate, service, event) or when a module is over- or under-modeled. Shaping a chosen one: ddd-distilled-value-objects, ddd-distilled-entities, ddd-distilled-aggregates. Area go or no-go: ddd-distilled-adoption-fit.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a change to existing code in small increments with the Domain-Driven Design Distilled order: subdomain, context, language, smallest pattern, boundaries, scenarios, spikes and deferred debt.
entries.argumentHint: [task description | issue text | path | empty to plan the work in the current diff]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Domain-Driven Design Distilled rule set to design and coding decisions in business software. Use for any task that creates, reviews or changes domain code where subdomain importance, bounded contexts, ubiquitous language or the cost of tactical patterns matters.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Domain-Driven Design Distilled rules and report ranked findings.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: subdomains
entries.description: Use when ranking areas of a business system as core, supporting or generic, or when the best modeling effort seems spent on a commodity concern. Covers classification, effort allocation and signs the core has drifted. Not for the go or no-go on DDD (ddd-distilled-adoption-fit).

entries.name: ubiquitous-language
entries.description: Use when naming or renaming concepts inside one context, when one concept has several names or one name two meanings there, or when names are placeholders such as Data, Info or Manager. Words: hidden decisions ddd-distilled-explicit-concepts; cross-context drift ddd-distilled-bounded-contexts.

entries.name: value-objects
entries.description: Use when a primitive or small group of fields (amount and currency, email, date range) is validated or combined in several places. Covers immutable, self-validating values. Flags and status codes: ddd-distilled-explicit-concepts; pattern undecided: ddd-distilled-pattern-economy.

entries.name: mode-context-first
entries.description: Opens every substantive answer with a context card (subdomain class, bounded context, local terms, foreign terms to translate) before any design or code.

entries.name: mode-earned-pattern
entries.description: Tags every tactical pattern it introduces with the reason it earns its cost, defaults to plain code, and lists the patterns considered and rejected.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Domain-Driven Design Distilled rule behind each decision and checks understanding.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps with the user, asking before any change larger than a few lines or touching public API, a context boundary or a published name.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against the Domain-Driven Design Distilled review rules, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Gives the result first in a few lines with no preamble, applying Domain-Driven Design Distilled quietly and showing failing output in full.

entries.name: aggregate-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of aggregate boundaries. Use proactively after edits that add children, references or collections to an aggregate, or that load object graphs, to check that each boundary follows a stated invariant and stays small.

entries.name: behavior-mover
entries.description: Implementer that moves a business decision from a service, controller or helper into the entity, value object or policy that should own it. Use when findings show an anemic model or a service holding business rules and changes were requested.

entries.name: ceremony-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of tactical pattern use in both directions. Use proactively after edits that add aggregates, events, repositories, translators or value objects, or that leave complex rules in plain data, to judge whether each pattern earns its cost. Hidden primitives and flags go to ddd-distilled-concept-reviewer.

entries.name: concept-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of hidden domain concepts. Use proactively after edits that add boolean parameters, status codes, enums, magic strings, helper methods or repeated primitive groups that carry business rules, to propose the concept that should replace them. Pattern cost per concept is ddd-distilled-ceremony-reviewer's.

entries.name: consistency-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of transaction scope across aggregates. Use proactively after edits to use cases, handlers or transaction code that load or save more than one aggregate root, or that add follow-up effects after a change.

entries.name: context-boundary-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of bounded context ownership. Use proactively after edits that add or change shared domain types, cross-module imports, or terms used in several modules, to find context bleeding and one model serving unrelated concerns. Judges a diff; for the whole repository use ddd-distilled-map-contexts.

entries.name: domain-test-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of tests of domain code. Use proactively after edits that add or change value objects, transitions, aggregates, services or translators, to check coverage per layer and whether tests read in the ubiquitous language.

entries.name: domain-test-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests in the ubiquitous language for value objects, transitions, orchestration and translation. Use when existing domain code has test gaps or new behavior needs tests; edits tests only. Not for a value object or translator introduced in the same task (their builders write those tests).

entries.name: entity-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of entities. Use proactively after edits that add or change classes with identity or lifecycle, public setters on business fields, or classes that are only getters and setters, to check explicit identity and guarded transitions. Judges the class itself; a decision found in a service goes to ddd-distilled-service-reviewer.

entries.name: event-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of domain events. Use proactively after edits that add, rename or publish events, to find noise events, command-like names, vague or mirror payloads and events raised outside the model.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Domain-Driven Design Distilled review checklist against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence. Use before declaring work done, committing or opening a pull request.

entries.name: infrastructure-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of infrastructure leaking into the model. Use proactively after edits to domain code that import frameworks, ORM, HTTP or serialization types, or that shape classes after tables or API payloads.

entries.name: integration-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of integration style choices. Use proactively after edits that add or change RPC calls, REST resources, queue consumers, webhooks or published events, to check coupling and failure semantics, contract separation and consumer safety.

entries.name: language-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of ubiquitous language in a change. Use proactively after edits that add or rename types, methods, events, commands or tests, to find synonyms, homonyms, technical placeholders and untranslated foreign terms.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Domain-Driven Design Distilled work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review to decide which specialists and skills apply, in at most five steps, and how much modeling the change earns. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: relationship-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of relationships between contexts and the translation at their edges. Use proactively after edits that add integrations, clients, adapters or mappers, to find silent conformism, name-only anticorruption layers, ungoverned shared kernels and untested translation. Judges a diff; for the whole repository use ddd-distilled-map-contexts.

entries.name: service-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of application services and controllers. Use proactively after edits to service, handler or controller code, to find business decisions that belong in the model, transport-shaped signatures and duplicated orchestration. Judges where decisions sit; the receiving class's own guards are ddd-distilled-entity-reviewer's.

entries.name: subdomain-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of modeling effort against subdomain importance. Use proactively after edits that add or deepen modules, or when a change touches areas of different business weight, to find over-invested commodity code and under-modeled core code.

entries.name: term-renamer
entries.description: Implementer that applies an already decided domain term rename across code, tests, events and documentation. Use when a language review or the business has settled a term and changes were requested; public names are listed, not changed.

entries.name: translation-builder
entries.description: Implementer that builds a translator and its tests at one context boundary and moves foreign types behind it. Use when findings show a foreign model, payload or schema leaking into local code and changes were requested.

entries.name: value-object-introducer
entries.description: Implementer that replaces a repeated primitive group with a value object in small, test-backed steps. Use when review findings or a plan call for introducing a value object for one concept.

entries.name: aggregate-boundaries
entries.description: Use when designing or reviewing what belongs inside one aggregate: its size, members, invariants, or an aggregate shaped like an ORM object graph. Inside one aggregate only. Outside access is aggregate-root-discipline; links between aggregates are cross-aggregate-coordination.

entries.name: aggregate-root-discipline
entries.description: Use when code outside an aggregate sets its fields, mutates child entities, receives its child collections or navigates through its internals. Judges the access surface; where the deciding code lives is application-services or domain-services. Size is aggregate-boundaries; life cycle is entities.

entries.name: anticorruption-layer
entries.description: Use when code consumes a legacy system, vendor or partner API, or another context's model, and foreign names, status codes or schemas appear in local domain code. Builds and tests the inbound translation. Outbound messages are integration-contracts; choosing the relationship is context-mapping.

entries.name: application-services
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing use-case code in a modeled area: a service or handler that loads, calls, saves and publishes, or whose branching on business state keeps growing. Thin orchestration and transactions. Decisions over several domain objects are domain-services; persistence is repositories.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for Implementing Domain-Driven Design health and return ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: bounded-context
entries.description: Use when deciding which bounded context code belongs to, when one class or enum is used by several contexts, or when a model looks shared or global. Owns ownership and validity of a model. Folder layout is module-structure; data leaving a context is integration-contracts.

entries.name: ceremony-check
entries.description: Plan, for named areas (paths, contexts or subdomain names), what to keep, trim or extract so the modeling matches the complexity there, with evidence per signal. Reads whole areas, not a diff; reviewing a diff is the ddd-implementing-modeling-effort-reviewer agent.
entries.argumentHint: [areas: paths, contexts or subdomain names | empty for the areas in the current diff]

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the Implementing Domain-Driven Design review checklist interactively: ten source questions plus five compact additions, each answered yes, no or not applicable with a next action.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: client-representations
entries.description: Use when a UI, REST endpoint, report or other client needs data shaped differently from an aggregate: serializing aggregates, per-client DTOs, projections, read models, query/command split, owner scope. Clients of this application; other contexts are integration-contracts; storage is repositories.

entries.name: context-map
entries.description: Reconstruct the context map of a codebase as found: contexts, relationships, translation points and leaks, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: context-mapping
entries.description: Use when two bounded contexts, a legacy system or a partner exchange data or terms, or when no one can say who translates between them. Decides the relationship, influence and translation ownership. The translator is anticorruption-layer; the outgoing message shape is integration-contracts.

entries.name: core-domain-focus
entries.description: Use when deciding how much DDD modeling an area deserves: plain CRUD or reference data wrapped in aggregates and events, or real lifecycle and invariants kept as flat records and scripts. Rules for core-domain effort and against DDD theater. Not one service's thickness (application-services).

entries.name: cross-aggregate-coordination
entries.description: Use when an aggregate holds or loads another aggregate, or one use case saves several aggregates in a single transaction. Identity references, one aggregate per transaction, eventual coordination. Not for the inside of one aggregate (aggregate-boundaries).

entries.name: domain-events
entries.description: Use when naming, shaping, raising or reviewing a domain event: past-tense facts, payload, and events that are really commands or property changes. Events as model facts. Messages leaving a context are integration-contracts; event-based persistence is event-sourcing.

entries.name: domain-services
entries.description: Use when a domain operation needs several domain objects and fits no single entity or value object, or when a class with a domain-sounding name only maps between schemas. Domain layer only; load-call-save use-case code is application-services; a rule on one entity belongs on that entity.

entries.name: domain-tests
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing tests of domain code: aggregate invariants, state transitions, value objects, domain events, repositories, translators and application services. Says what each layer's test asserts and what it leaves out.

entries.name: entities
entries.description: Use when designing or reviewing a class that has identity and a life cycle: status fields, setters, state transitions, or an ORM-mapped class with no behavior. Covers identity, transitions and domain verbs. Outside access is aggregate-root-discipline; attribute-defined types are value-objects.

entries.name: event-sourcing
entries.description: Use when deciding whether to persist an aggregate as its sequence of events, or when writing or reviewing event streams, replay, event versions or upcasters. Storage by events only. Events as announced facts, with or without sourcing, are domain-events.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Implementing Domain-Driven Design rule: its strength, the reason, how to check it in code, a small example and where it bends.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | section name | question about a rule]

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve named Implementing Domain-Driven Design findings with the smallest change that fixes each, run the tests after every step, and never commit.
entries.argumentHint: [findings text | review output | finding ids | empty to fix the findings above]

entries.name: integration-contracts
entries.description: Use when data leaves a bounded context for another: a message, event payload, API response, identifier, or another context reading its tables. Shapes the outbound contract model. Inbound is anticorruption-layer; who owns a class is bounded-context; UI and API clients are client-representations.

entries.name: invariant-inventory
entries.description: List the invariants of an aggregate or use case, decide which must hold immediately and which may be eventual, and propose or defend the aggregate boundary or transaction scope with that evidence.
entries.argumentHint: [aggregate or class | use case | empty to ask or use the diff]

entries.name: model-walk
entries.description: Walk a new domain concept through the nine code-generation steps and produce a model sheet before any code: context, terms, tactical types, aggregate boundary, references, invariants, repositories, services, translations.
entries.argumentHint: [concept or feature description | issue text | empty to ask]

entries.name: module-structure
entries.description: Use when laying out or moving folders, packages or modules: a layer-only tree, a shared or common package, or directory names that hide the model. Layout only. Which context owns a class is bounded-context; what crosses between contexts is integration-contracts.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a change to existing DDD code: context, edit order, tests first, boundary and transaction decisions, hand-offs and stop conditions. Plans only.
entries.argumentHint: [change request | issue text | empty to plan from the current diff]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Implementing Domain-Driven Design rule set to code that models a business domain. Use for any task on bounded contexts, aggregates, repositories, domain events, application services or cross-context integration, and to find the right specialist.

entries.name: repositories
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing a repository interface or implementation: one per aggregate root, its methods, what it returns, and whether business rules or ORM rows leak through it. Persistence contract only. Client read models are client-representations; use-case code is application-services.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Implementing Domain-Driven Design rules and report ranked findings, each mapped to the skill that treats it.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: ubiquitous-language
entries.description: Use when naming or renaming a class, method, event, test or package, when one concept has several names, or when one term carries two meanings inside the same context. Keeps one local term per concept. Which context owns a term is bounded-context.

entries.name: value-objects
entries.description: Use when raw primitives such as strings, numbers, dates or ids carry business meaning, when a small value class is mutable or unvalidated, or when equality of a descriptive type is by identity. Immutable, validated, value-equal types. Identity and life cycle are entities.

entries.name: mode-context-first
entries.description: Opens every design or code answer with the bounded context, its local terms and its relationship to neighbors, and asks one question when the context is unknown.

entries.name: mode-invariant-first
entries.description: Before any change to an aggregate, a transaction or an event, prints the invariants, the boundary decision and the transaction scope, then makes the change.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Implementing Domain-Driven Design rule behind each decision, names its strength and provenance, and checks understanding with one question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps and asks before changing an aggregate boundary, a transaction scope, a published contract or anything past a few lines.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against the Implementing Domain-Driven Design rules, does not rewrite code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first, no preamble, a few lines at most unless asked, while still reporting what ran, any unresolved risk, and failing output in full.

entries.name: acl-builder
entries.description: Implementer that wraps a legacy, vendor, partner or other-context model behind a narrow port in local language with a translator and its tests, then migrates callers one at a time. Use when reviews find foreign types, status codes or schemas inside domain or application code.

entries.name: aggregate-design-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of aggregate shape: size, which invariant justifies each member, ORM-shaped object graphs, and object references to other aggregates instead of identities. Use proactively after edits that add an aggregate, a child entity or collection, or a field typed as another aggregate.

entries.name: context-boundary-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of context ownership and layout: which bounded context each changed file belongs to, shared or common domain packages, global models, boundaries that exist only in diagrams, and package structure. Use proactively after edits that add packages, move files or share a class between contexts.

entries.name: domain-test-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests for domain code by layer: invariants, transitions, value objects, events as outcomes, translators, repositories and application-service orchestration, in the ubiquitous language. Writes tests only; never edits production code. Use when reviews find missing or misplaced tests.

entries.name: event-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of domain events: past-tense facts versus commands, events emitted per property change, payloads with framework or persistence types, repair events, and publication order. Use proactively after edits that add an event class, a publish call or a subscriber.

entries.name: event-sourcing-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of event-sourced aggregates: whether sourcing is justified, stream identity and versioning, deterministic replay, event versions and upcasters. Use proactively after edits that add or change an event store, an apply method, a stream append or a stored event shape. Not applicable without stored events.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Implementing Domain-Driven Design review checklist (ten questions plus five compact additions) against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence. Use when work is about to be declared done, committed or opened as a pull request.

entries.name: identity-reference-converter
entries.description: Implementer that replaces object references between aggregates with identity references in small test-backed steps, and moves an unrelated member of an oversized aggregate into its own aggregate once the invariants are listed. Use when reviews find held aggregates or ORM-shaped aggregates.

entries.name: language-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of ubiquitous language: synonyms for one concept, one term with two meanings, technical placeholders, foreign vocabulary, and names in tests, events and packages that drift from the model. Use proactively after edits that add or rename domain classes, events, commands or tests.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Implementing Domain-Driven Design work. Use when starting any non-trivial change or review to decide which reviewers, skills and (only when edits were requested) implementers apply, in what order, in at most five steps. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: modeling-effort-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of modeling effort per area: DDD patterns on trivial CRUD, vocabulary without design change, vendor terms in the core, and real lifecycle complexity left in service branching. Use proactively after edits that add aggregates, repositories or events, or that grow a service full of status checks.

entries.name: repository-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of repository contracts: one per aggregate root, method shape, return types, generic CRUD bases, ORM rows leaking out and business rules inside implementations. Use proactively after edits that add or change a repository interface, its implementation or its callers.

entries.name: representation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of what clients receive and ask for: aggregates or rows serialized to APIs and views, one DTO for every client, load-and-stitch reads, domain annotations for the wire, and implicit tenant or owner scope. Use proactively after edits to controllers, endpoints, DTOs, queries or reports.

entries.name: root-discipline-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of aggregate access paths: public setters, returned mutable collections, child entities held outside the root, and callers that read state and write it back. Use proactively after edits to entities, aggregate roots or the code that calls them.

entries.name: root-encapsulator
entries.description: Implementer that moves invariant-changing logic behind aggregate root methods and closes setters and exposed collections, one finding at a time with tests. Use when reviews find outside code mutating aggregate internals, or services and controllers holding rules the root should own.

entries.name: rule-placement-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of where business decisions live: model, domain service, application service, controller or repository. Finds branching rules in the wrong layer, duplicated invariants, behavior parked in services, and mappers posing as domain services. Use proactively after edits to services, handlers or controllers.

entries.name: test-coverage-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of domain test coverage: maps each changed domain behavior to the layer of test the rules call for (invariant, transition, value, event, repository, translator, application service) and finds gaps and misplaced tests. Use proactively after edits to domain code, or before a pull request.

entries.name: transaction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of transaction scope in use cases: how many aggregates each transaction saves, the invariant that justifies it, and whether cross-aggregate reactions run in their own transactions. Use proactively after edits to application services, handlers or units of work.

entries.name: transaction-splitter
entries.description: Implementer that splits a use case saving several aggregates into one transaction per aggregate, coordinated by a past-tense domain event and a repeat-safe policy, after the invariants are listed and the delay is accepted. Use when a review finds a wide transaction with no immediate invariant behind it.

entries.name: translation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of boundary crossings: every place a model enters or leaves a context or system, in which direction, as which type, and where it is translated. Use proactively after edits that call another context, a legacy or vendor system, publish messages, or share enums or tables.

entries.name: value-object-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of value types and primitive obsession: meaningful primitives in signatures and fields, mutable or unvalidated value classes, identity-compared values, and rules copied across callers. Use proactively after edits that add parameters, identifiers, amounts, ranges or small data classes.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture health and return one rating per pattern family and ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: base-patterns
entries.description: Use for small supporting patterns: money held in floats, repeated null checks, a global registry or service locator, a shared base class, plug-in selection, an interface beside its implementation, tabular data passed as objects. Wrapping external systems is integration-boundaries.

entries.name: blocker-scan
entries.description: Hunt the six forbidden patterns (layering theater, generic repository, ORM-driven everything, controller-centric app, distributed object fantasy, unclear transaction ownership) over a tree and return instances in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: build-feature
entries.description: Implement a new enterprise use case slice by slice in the book's generation order (pattern, service, domain, persistence, transaction, boundary DTOs, presentation) with tests at each responsibility. Runs the tests and never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [use case description | plan reference | empty to ask]

entries.name: business-logic-patterns
entries.description: Use when deciding where business rules live: choosing Transaction Script, Table Module or Domain Model, noticing a script growing duplicated rules, or an anemic model beside a fat service. Decisions about the business only; use-case sequencing is service-layer.

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture review checklist against the current work, answering yes, no or not applicable with evidence and a next step for each no. Interactive and read-only.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: choose-pattern
entries.description: Turn a feature or code situation into forces, then recommend the smallest fitting enterprise pattern per decision (business logic, data access, transactions, presentation, remote, session), with rejected alternatives and an escalation trigger.
entries.argumentHint: [situation or feature | file | empty to ask]

entries.name: data-mapper
entries.description: Use when storage knowledge leaks into domain objects (SQL, column names or ORM base classes in the model), mapping code is repeated in callers, or you must decide if a Data Mapper is worth it. Interface shape is repository; coupled options are gateways-and-active-record.

entries.name: escalate-pattern
entries.description: When a Transaction Script has outgrown itself (duplicated decisions, lifecycle or invariant complexity), confirm the trigger, move the most repeated decision into a model object in small tested steps, and name the persistence follow-up.
entries.argumentHint: [file | function | file:line | empty to ask]

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture rule or pattern: its strength (must, should, must not), the force behind it, how to check it, an original example and the book's own exceptions.
entries.argumentHint: [rule or pattern name | section | situation you are unsure about]

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture findings with the smallest change per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: gateways-and-active-record
entries.description: Use when choosing a persistence pattern for simple or table-shaped work: Row Data Gateway, Table Data Gateway or Active Record, a report building objects per row, or Active Record spreading into a complex domain. Decoupled domains use data-mapper and repository.

entries.name: inheritance-mapping
entries.description: Use when a class hierarchy has to be persisted: choosing between one table for the hierarchy, a table per class, or a table per concrete class, or when domain code branches on a discriminator column. Not for associations or values; see relational-mapping-structure.

entries.name: integration-boundaries
entries.description: Use when code consumes a partner, vendor or legacy system: foreign field names, status codes or SDK types spread through the app, messages used as domain objects, or serialization code with rules in it. Call counts and your own remote API are remote-boundaries.

entries.name: layering
entries.description: Use for the split into presentation, application, domain and data-access layers, or imports and return types that cross layers: domain code importing a web framework, a repository returning response shapes, forwarding-only layers. Not handler content (presentation-layer) or service design.

entries.name: loading-behavior
entries.description: Use when objects are loaded: the same row appears as two live objects, an association is lazy-loaded inside a loop, serializer or template, or a list endpoint issues one query per row (N+1). Reads and identity; commit scope is transactions-and-unit-of-work.

entries.name: offline-locking
entries.description: Use when two users or sessions can edit the same data across separate requests: lost updates, a version column, row locks held between requests, locks on related objects, or stale locks. One request's commit scope is transactions-and-unit-of-work.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a non-trivial enterprise change in the book's generation order, with an explicit transaction owner, test plan and a list of patterns you will not add. Produces a plan only; no edits.
entries.argumentHint: [feature or change description | file:line | empty to ask]

entries.name: presentation-layer
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing what sits inside handlers, controllers, views, templates or presentation models: business rules, SQL or transactions in them, display formatting in domain code, one type as form, entity and response. Imports are layering; pattern choice is web-presentation-patterns.

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture rule set to enterprise code. Use for any task that places business logic, persistence, transactions, locking, presentation, integration, session state or remote boundaries, or that reviews such code.

entries.name: query-and-metadata-mapping
entries.description: Use when SQL strings are built in several places, search filters are combined at runtime, or mapping rules are driven by configuration, annotations or reflection. Covers Query Object and Metadata Mapping. Finder interfaces are repository; table layout is relational-mapping-structure.

entries.name: relational-mapping-structure
entries.description: Use when designing or reviewing how objects map to tables: keys and identity fields, object references, many-to-many links, owned child rows, small values in the parent row, serialized blob columns. Hierarchies are inheritance-mapping; queries and mapping config are query-and-metadata-mapping.

entries.name: remote-boundaries
entries.description: Use when your own API or client makes several calls per user action, objects are exposed remotely method by method, domain classes appear in responses, or a service split is proposed. Covers Remote Facade, DTOs, distribution rules. Partner payloads are integration-boundaries.

entries.name: remote-contract
entries.description: Design a coarse remote operation for a consumer need: the single call, request and response DTOs, the domain-to-DTO translation, versioning rule, failure behavior and a before-and-after call count. Produces a contract; no edits.
entries.argumentHint: [consumer need or screen | endpoint file | empty to ask]

entries.name: repository
entries.description: Use when defining or reviewing the interface domain or application code uses to read and store objects: a generic CRUD repository, finders shaped by columns, callers building queries. Mapping code is data-mapper; gateways and Active Record are gateways-and-active-record.

entries.name: responsibility-map
entries.description: Map who owns each of the seven enterprise responsibilities (presentation, workflow, domain, data access, transactions, concurrency, integration) for a use case or package, and list collisions in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [use case | file | directory | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture rules and report ranked findings, with forbidden patterns as blockers.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: service-layer
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing application services or use-case classes: a controller orchestrating several steps, a service that holds every rule or only forwards to persistence, an API shaped by UI mechanics. Not for rule placement (business-logic-patterns) or layer imports (layering).

entries.name: session-state
entries.description: Use when per-user state must survive between requests: cookies or tokens carrying data, server-held sessions, a session table, expiry and cleanup, a cart or wizard lost on restart. Shared-record edit conflicts are offline-locking; UI state in domain code is presentation-layer.

entries.name: testing-by-responsibility
entries.description: Use when writing or placing tests for enterprise code: a business rule tested only through HTTP or a database, mappers or repositories mocked away, transaction or locking behavior untested, remote mapping uncovered, or a real remote service needed to run tests.

entries.name: transactions-and-unit-of-work
entries.description: Use when deciding who opens and commits a transaction, saves are scattered across callers, an ORM flushes at surprising times, or a remote call sits inside a transaction. One request's commit scope; cross-request edits are offline-locking, reads are loading-behavior.

entries.name: web-presentation-patterns
entries.description: Use when choosing how requests are handled and responses rendered: Page Controller or Front Controller, Template View, Transform View or Two Step View, MVC roles, or a multi-step flow whose navigation is scattered. What handlers may contain is presentation-layer.

entries.name: mode-force-first
entries.description: Before any design or code, states the forces in play, the smallest enterprise pattern that fits, the alternative rejected and the trigger that would change the choice.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the enterprise pattern behind each decision, names the force that chose it, and ends non-trivial answers with one check question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps in the book's generation order, runs the tests after each, and asks before any change larger than a few lines or touching a public API, schema or transaction boundary.

entries.name: mode-request-path
entries.description: Starts every design or change by drawing the request path across layers, marking who owns the transaction, where data is read and written, and every remote hop, then repeats the path after the change.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Responds with a ranked findings table against the enterprise pattern rules, treats forbidden patterns as blockers, and does not rewrite code unless asked.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Gives the result first in a few lines, with no preamble, the pattern chosen in at most a clause, and failing output shown in full.

entries.name: base-pattern-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of small supporting patterns: float money, repeated null handling, registries and service locators, speculative base classes, interfaces beside implementations, plug-in selection and row objects nobody uses. Use proactively after edits that add base classes, registries, money or value types.

entries.name: facade-builder
entries.description: Implementer that builds a coarse remote operation: a facade method, request and response DTOs and assemblers over existing application services, with boundary tests. Use when a remote contract or review finding calls for replacing chatty or entity-shaped endpoints.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture review checklist and the six forbidden patterns against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence. Use before declaring work done, committing or opening a pull request.

entries.name: integration-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how external and partner systems are consumed: vendor or partner types and field names outside one gateway, internal design shaped by payloads, messages used as domain objects, rules inside serializers, and untranslated errors. Use proactively after edits that call or receive from another system.

entries.name: layering-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of layer assignment and dependency direction: domain or data-access code importing web types, repositories returning response shapes, layers that only forward calls, unassigned files. Handler and view content is enterprise-patterns-presentation-reviewer. Use proactively after edits that add classes, imports or a new layer.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for enterprise application architecture work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review to decide which specialist reviewers, implementers and skills apply, in what order, and which patterns not to add. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: loading-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how objects are loaded: queries per row (N+1), lazy associations touched in loops, serializers or templates, duplicate in-memory objects for one row, and expensive joins hidden behind traversal. Use proactively after edits to list endpoints, mappers, serializers or model associations.

entries.name: lock-adder
entries.description: Implementer that adds an optimistic offline lock to one entity: version field, conditional update, named conflict error, conflict mapping at the edge and an interleaved-edit test. Use when a review finds last-write-wins updates on shared, user-edited data.

entries.name: lock-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of concurrent-edit handling: last-write-wins updates, missing or ignored version checks, locks held across requests or think time, stale locks, groups edited as one without a shared lock, and invisible implicit locking. Use proactively after edits to update paths for shared data.

entries.name: logic-mover
entries.description: Implementer that moves a business decision out of a handler, script, SQL, DTO or serializer into the object, function or layer that owns it, in small test-backed steps. Use when review findings or a plan name misplaced or duplicated business rules.

entries.name: logic-placement-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of where business decisions live and whether the business logic pattern fits: rules in controllers, views, SQL or DTOs, rules trapped in growing scripts, anemic models in rich domains, or trivial CRUD over-modeled. Use proactively after edits that add or change business conditions.

entries.name: mapping-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of object-relational structure: keys and identity fields, foreign keys, association tables, owned child rows, embedded values, serialized blobs, inheritance strategy, scattered SQL fragments and mapping metadata. Use proactively after edits to schemas, migrations, mappers or ORM mappings.

entries.name: persistence-extractor
entries.description: Implementer that extracts SQL, row mapping or storage detail from handlers, services or domain classes behind a repository, mapper or gateway shaped by use-case questions, in small test-backed steps. Use when review findings name data access in the wrong place.

entries.name: persistence-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of data access design: generic or table-shaped repositories, SQL outside data-access code, domain objects that know storage, Active Record in complex domains, and one class serving as row, entity and response. Use proactively after edits to repositories, mappers, gateways or models.

entries.name: presentation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the presentation edge: business rules, SQL or transactions inside handlers, views and templates, one type reused as form, entity and response, display formatting in domain code, pattern fit. Import direction is enterprise-patterns-layering-reviewer. Use proactively after edits to controllers, handlers, views or templates.

entries.name: remote-api-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the application's own remote boundaries: many calls per user action, object-shaped or fine-grained operations, domain classes on the wire, missing DTO translation, and callers that treat network calls as local.
