Use proactively after edits to endpoints, API clients or service splits.

entries.name: service-layer-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of application services and use-case classes: naming by table or screen, UI mechanics in signatures, services that forward calls or swallow all domain logic, and duplicated orchestration across callers. Use proactively after edits to service or use-case classes.

entries.name: session-state-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of state kept between requests: client-held values that drive decisions, session data with no owner or expiry, in-memory sessions on several instances, domain objects stored in sessions, and unclear failover. Use proactively after edits to cookies, tokens, session stores or wizard state.

entries.name: test-alignment-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of test placement: business rules tested only through HTTP or a database, mocked-away data access, workflows without commit and rollback tests, locks without conflict tests, boundary mapping untested. Use proactively after edits that add behavior or change tests.

entries.name: test-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests at the layer that owns each behavior: domain rules without a database, data-access round trips, workflow commit and rollback, interleaved edits, boundary mapping and gateway stubs. Use when a change adds behavior or a review shows misplaced or missing tests.

entries.name: transaction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of transaction ownership and write coordination: commits in helpers, ad hoc saves, remote calls inside a transaction, surprising ORM flush timing, and workflows held in one transaction. Use proactively after edits that save, commit, open sessions or call other systems.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for refactoring readiness: where change is expensive, whether the area has a safety net, and which smells cost most. Ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: behavior-preservation
entries.description: Use to decide whether a change really is a refactoring: what counts as observable behavior, a feature or bug fix hiding inside cleanup, a risky 'modernization'. Judges the meaning of a change; step size is small-steps, tests are safety-net, packaging is patch-hygiene.

entries.name: call-signatures
entries.description: Use when a function has many parameters, boolean flags that switch behavior, an argument order callers must memorize, or repeated argument groups. Reshapes the call, not the types behind it (primitive-obsession) or the function body (function-bodies).

entries.name: characterize
entries.description: Pin the current behavior of unclear code with characterization tests before refactoring it. Writes or edits test files only; never touches production code.
entries.argumentHint: [file | function | module | empty to use the files in the current diff]

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the final Refactoring checklist against the current work in the session and give a concrete next action for every item that is not yet a yes.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: conditionals
entries.description: Use when branching inside one function is hard to read: nested if/else, repeated or compound conditions, control flags, a tempting lookup table. Local branch structure and restraint; repetition by kind is variation-and-state, failure branches are error-paths.

entries.name: duplication
entries.description: Use when the same logic appears in several places, a fix had to be made twice, or someone proposes a utils or common module. Merge copies of one piece of knowledge into one owner; leave coincidental similarity alone. Removing a layer is needless-abstraction.

entries.name: error-paths
entries.description: Use when error handling hides the main path, or a refactoring touches validation, cleanup, recovery, error codes or exceptions. Keeps failure behavior identical while making it readable. Ordinary branching is conditionals; cutting a function is function-bodies.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Refactoring rule, smell or catalog move: its strength, the reason, how to check it, an original example and the source's own limits.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | smell | catalog move | topic | empty to list topics]

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given refactoring findings with the smallest named move per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | row numbers | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: function-bodies
entries.description: Use when a function is long or mixes parsing, validation, computation and I/O, or when temporaries and expressions hide intent. Where to cut a function and the moves inside a body. Parameters are call-signatures; branch structure is conditionals.

entries.name: hidden-dependencies
entries.description: Use when code reads globals, singletons, the clock, environment, config or ambient request context, or a function has side effects its name hides. What code reads from outside its signature; who may write shared state is mutation-control.

entries.name: inheritance-moves
entries.description: Use when a hierarchy needs reshaping: duplicated or misplaced superclass members, inheritance used for reuse, empty layers, or two variation axes in one tree. Hierarchy mechanics only; constant-only subclasses are variation-and-state, forwarding layers needless-abstraction, placement ownership.

entries.name: mutation-control
entries.description: Use when state is public or changed from many places: exposed fields or collections, needless setters, duplicated update logic, bidirectional links. What others may write; what code reads from ambient state is hidden-dependencies.

entries.name: needless-abstraction
entries.description: Use when a class or layer only forwards calls, an interface has one implementation, a library has one caller, or code exists just in case. Removes weight that exists; merging copies is duplication, hierarchies are inheritance-moves, whether to keep cleaning is stopping-rules.

entries.name: ownership
entries.description: Use when one class changes for many reasons, one change edits many files, a method mostly works on another object's data, or domain rules sit in UI or I/O code. Where behavior lives among peers; types for concepts are primitive-obsession, hierarchies inheritance-moves.

entries.name: patch-hygiene
entries.description: Use when shaping a diff, commit series or pull request that mixes renames, code motion, redesign and logic changes, or is too big to review. Packaging and intent per patch; whether behavior actually changed is behavior-preservation.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a change to existing code in the book's order: friction, safety net, preparatory refactoring, the behavior change, follow-up cleanup and a stop condition. Plans only; edits nothing.
entries.argumentHint: [change request | ticket text | file:function | empty to infer from the current diff]

entries.name: preparatory-steps
entries.description: Use when a requested feature or bug fix is awkward to add in the current structure: ask what makes it awkward, reshape locally first, then change behavior, then clean up. Bound to one upcoming change; general step discipline is small-steps.

entries.name: prepare
entries.description: Do only the preparatory refactoring for a stated change: at most five verified behavior-preserving steps that make the change straightforward, then hand back before the behavior change.
entries.argumentHint: [the change you are about to make | ticket text | empty to ask]

entries.name: primitive-obsession
entries.description: Use when the same primitives travel together or carry rules: ids and codes as strings, parallel fields, positional arrays, magic values. Introduces named types; call shape is call-signatures, which class owns behavior is ownership.

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Refactoring rule set (behavior-preserving structural change in small, tested steps) to any task that changes existing code. Use first for feature work, bug fixes, cleanup and review of existing code; it routes to the specific skill, agent or mode.

entries.name: renaming
entries.description: Use when names hide intent, describe mechanism, or disagree with domain terms, or a rename is proposed. Safe renames and how far to take them in one change. No other skill rewrites identifiers; the packaging of a large rename is patch-hygiene.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Refactoring rules and report ranked findings, starting with whether the change keeps behavior, one intent and a safety net.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: safety-net
entries.description: Use before risky structural edits, or when tests are absent, weak or being edited during a refactoring: finding or building a safety net, characterization tests, keeping tests honest. The tests that prove behavior; judging the change's meaning is behavior-preservation.

entries.name: small-steps
entries.description: Use when planning or doing a structural change and tempted to rewrite or change a lot at once: step size, reversibility, runnable states, order of work. Not meaning (behavior-preservation), when to stop (stopping-rules) or the moment before a feature (preparatory-steps).

entries.name: smell-to-refactoring
entries.description: Confirm smells in a scope and map each to the smallest named catalog move, its precondition, safety net and stop condition, ranked, in at most 40 lines. Includes a leave-it-alone verdict.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | file | glob | empty for the files in the current diff]

entries.name: split-patch
entries.description: Turn a mixed diff into an ordered series of single-intent patches (renames, moves, preparation, behavior) and say which hunks belong to each. Plans the split; does not stage or commit.
entries.argumentHint: [git ref | paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: stopping-rules
entries.description: Use when deciding whether to keep cleaning: the change is already easy, the smell is gone, the next abstraction is speculative, or cleanup looks like theater. When to stop, not how to proceed (small-steps); removing existing layers is needless-abstraction.

entries.name: variation-and-state
entries.description: Use when the same type code, status or mode is switched on in several places, subclasses only override constants, repeated null checks share one meaning, fields are set only on some paths, or creation needs a name. Variation across the code; one local branch is conditionals.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Refactoring rule or smell behind each choice, names the catalog move used, and ends non-trivial answers with one check-for-understanding question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps with tests between them, and asks before any change larger than a few lines or touching a public name.

entries.name: mode-prep-first
entries.description: Runs every change task in the book's order and reports it as a fixed sequence: friction, safety net, preparation, change, follow-up cleanup, and the reason it stopped.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against the Refactoring rules, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly when clean.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Gives the result first with no preamble, in at most a few lines unless more is asked, while still showing failing test output in full.

entries.name: mode-two-hats
entries.description: Tags every edit as STRUCTURE or BEHAVIOR, never both in one step, and announces each switch of hat so structural changes and behavior changes stay separable.

entries.name: abstraction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that builds an evidence table for each abstraction in changed code (interfaces, wrappers, factories, strategies, shared modules) and judges keep or inline. Use proactively after edits that add an interface, layer, wrapper or common module.

entries.name: behavior-preservation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that builds a behavior-delta ledger for a change claimed to preserve behavior: the observable surface of each touched unit, marked same, changed or unknown. Use proactively after edits described as cleanup, rename, move or refactoring.

entries.name: class-splitter
entries.description: Implementer that splits one class that changes for several reasons into cohesive classes, one field or method at a time, tests between steps. Use when an ownership review names a god class and changes were requested.

entries.name: conditional-refactorer
entries.description: Implementer that replaces repeated type-based branching with a table, strategy or polymorphism only when the repetition justifies it, and removes modeling added for a single branch. Use when a conditional review names a repeated type or status switch and changes were requested.

entries.name: conditional-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that inventories branches and type switches in changed code and gives each a proportionate verdict, including leave-as-is. Use proactively after edits that add branches, switch on a type or status, or introduce polymorphism or strategies.

entries.name: dependency-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that inventories hidden inputs and effects in changed code: globals, singletons, clock, environment, config and ambient context, plus side effects a name hides. Use proactively after edits that add ambient reads or effects to business logic.

entries.name: duplication-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of duplication decisions: groups repeated logic into clusters and judges whether each is one piece of knowledge to merge, coincidence to leave, or a merge made too early. Use proactively after edits that copy a block, add a utils module or extract shared code.

entries.name: error-path-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that compares error behavior before and after a change, exit by exit: error type, message, timing relative to side effects, cleanup, logging and recovery. Use proactively after edits that restructure validation, try/catch, cleanup or error returns.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Refactoring review checklist and forbidden patterns against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence per item. Use before declaring work done, committing or opening a pull request.

entries.name: friction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that compares a finished change with the friction it was meant to remove, and returns a stop-rule verdict: friction removed, not removed, or cleanup overshot. Use proactively after a refactoring or a feature with preparatory cleanup, before the final gate.

entries.name: function-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of function bodies: where to cut, mixed phases and abstraction levels, reused temporaries, parameter reassignment, and over-extraction. Use proactively after edits that add or lengthen functions or extract helpers.

entries.name: hierarchy-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that maps inheritance hierarchies touched by a change and names the move each problem suggests: pull up, push down, collapse, template method, delegation, or teasing apart axes. Use proactively after edits that add subclasses or change superclass members.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Refactoring work. Use first on any non-trivial change to existing code to decide, in at most five steps, which specialists and skills apply and in what order. Routes only; does not review the code itself.

entries.name: mutation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that lists the mutation surface of changed classes: public fields, setters, exposed collections, duplicated state transitions and association direction, with the writers of each. Use proactively after edits that add fields, setters or getters returning collections.

entries.name: ownership-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of where behavior and data live: classes that change for many reasons, changes that ripple across files, methods that envy another object's data, and domain rules in UI or I/O code. Use proactively after edits that add logic to an existing class.

entries.name: patch-intent-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that labels every hunk of a diff by intent (rename, move, extract-inline, prepare, behavior, test-for-behavior, format, unrelated) and gives a single-intent or mixed verdict. Use proactively before committing or opening a pull request, and when a diff is hard to review.

entries.name: primitive-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that finds recurring primitive bundles, loaded primitives and positional arrays in changed code and names the type each one implies, or says to leave it. Use proactively after edits that add parameters, ids, codes or tuple-shaped data.

entries.name: refactorer
entries.description: Implementer that carries out a list of refactoring findings or a plan as named behavior-preserving moves, running the tests between steps. Use when review findings or a plan span several functions or files and changes were requested.

entries.name: safety-net-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that maps the behavior a planned or finished refactoring touches to the tests that would catch a mistake, and says whether the net is ready. Use proactively before risky structural edits, or when a refactoring ships without new tests.

entries.name: signature-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of function signatures and call sites: long parameter lists, behavior-switching flags, argument-order traps, repeated argument groups and unpack-and-pass calls. Use proactively after edits that add or change parameters.

entries.name: test-change-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer that lists every test added, edited, skipped or deleted in a diff and judges each against preserved behavior. Use proactively after any refactoring that touches test files, or when a test was changed to make a change pass.

entries.name: value-type-introducer
entries.description: Implementer that introduces one named type for a recurring primitive bundle or loaded primitive and threads it inward from the boundary, keeping accepted input unchanged. Use when a primitive review names a concept and changes were requested.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for smells in the source's scan order, and return ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: behavior-ownership
entries.description: Use when a method works mostly on another object's data (feature envy), a class holds data while clients hold the logic (data class), or two classes depend on each other's internals (inappropriate intimacy). Decides where behavior belongs; the move itself is moving-features.

entries.name: change-locality
entries.description: Use when one change forces edits across many classes (shotgun surgery), one class changes for unrelated reasons (divergent change), or the same logic is repeated (duplicate code). Decides how to centralize or leave duplication; timing of the third copy is when-to-refactor.

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the ten Refactoring.Guru review questions interactively against the current work, with evidence and a next action for every no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: classify-change
entries.description: Label each hunk of a diff as refactoring, feature, bug fix or mixed, and propose an order and a split so structure and behavior are reviewed separately.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: composing-methods
entries.description: Use when about to perform Extract Method, Inline Method, Extract Variable, Inline Temp, Replace Temp with Query, Split Temporary Variable, Remove Assignments to Parameters, Method Object or Substitute Algorithm. Mechanics and safety checks, not diagnosis (size-smells).

entries.name: conditional-moves
entries.description: Use when about to perform Decompose Conditional, Consolidate Conditional Expression, Consolidate Duplicate Conditional Fragments, Remove Control Flag, guard clauses or Introduce Assertion. Checks side effects and order; polymorphic dispatch is in type-codes-and-switches.

entries.name: data-smells
entries.description: Use when primitives, arrays or magic numbers stand in for concepts, a signature has more than three or four parameters, or the same group of values travels together (primitive obsession, parameter list, data clumps). Diagnosis and choice; mechanics are in organizing-data and method-call-moves.

entries.name: dead-weight
entries.description: Use when code may be unused or not earning its cost: unused parameters, fields, methods, classes, near-empty classes, or abstractions built for imagined needs (dead code, lazy class, speculative generality). Decides deletion, inlining or keeping; reach checks are public-compatibility.

entries.name: debt-triage
entries.description: Rank known technical debt by its effect on current change speed, correctness and team understanding, and decide absorb now, schedule or accept for each item.
entries.argumentHint: [list of debt items | file | empty to use deferred smells and TODOs in the current diff]

entries.name: delegation-and-gaps
entries.description: Use when client code walks a chain of objects (message chains), a class only forwards calls (middle man), or a library class lacks an operation you keep working around (incomplete library class). Balances hiding delegates against removing layers; mechanics: moving-features.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Refactoring.Guru rule, smell or technique: its strength, the reason, how to check it, an original example and the source's own exception.
entries.argumentHint: [rule text | smell name | technique name | question]

entries.name: explanatory-comments
entries.description: Use when a comment explains what confusing code does, sits above a block that could be named, or guards a hidden assumption. Decides rename, extract variable, extract method or assertion versus keeping a comment for rationale; performing the extraction is composing-methods.

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve named refactoring findings one technique at a time with the smallest change, run the tests after each step, and never commit.
entries.argumentHint: [findings text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: hierarchies
entries.description: Use when a subclass ignores inherited members (refused bequest), two classes do one job with different interfaces, a new subclass forces a matching subclass elsewhere, or when pulling up, pushing down, extracting a superclass or interface, collapsing or replacing inheritance.

entries.name: method-call-moves
entries.description: Use when about to change a method's name or signature: Add or Remove Parameter, Separate Query from Modifier, Parameterize Method, explicit methods for a flag, Preserve Whole Object, Parameter Object, factory method, error code versus exception. Not diagnosis (data-smells).

entries.name: moving-features
entries.description: Use when about to perform Move Method, Move Field, Extract Class, Inline Class, Hide Delegate, Remove Middle Man, Introduce Foreign Method or Local Extension. Mechanics and safety checks, not diagnosis (behavior-ownership, delegation-and-gaps, size-smells).

entries.name: organizing-data
entries.description: Use when about to perform Replace Data Value with Object, change value to reference or back, Replace Array with Object, encapsulate a field or collection, change association direction, or replace a magic number. Identity and mutability decisions, then safe steps; not diagnosis (data-smells).

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a non-trivial change before editing: primary smell, cost, smallest refactoring, cleaner end state, stop condition, checks and ordering against feature work.
entries.argumentHint: [goal or ticket text | paths | empty to plan from the current diff]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Refactoring.Guru rule set to changes of existing code. Use when smells, technique choice, behavior preservation or cleanup scope matter; it routes to the narrower skills, agents and modes of this plugin.

entries.name: public-compatibility
entries.description: Use before deleting, renaming, inlining, hiding or changing the signature, constructor, visibility or type hierarchy of anything other code may reach: public, generated, reflected, serialized, plugin-facing or test-facing. Transition paths; candidates come from dead-weight.

entries.name: reachability-check
entries.description: For one symbol, parameter or file, search every way other code may reach it and return a verdict on whether deleting, renaming or changing it is safe, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: <symbol | file | function(param)> [change: delete | rename | change signature | hide | inline]

entries.name: refactoring-process
entries.description: Use when carrying out a refactoring: keeping it separate from feature or bug-fix edits, working in small steps, choosing and running checks, and judging whether the code got cleaner. Not for deciding whether to refactor now (when-to-refactor).

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Refactoring.Guru rules and report ranked findings with a disposition for each.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: size-smells
entries.description: Use when a method needs scrolling or comments to follow, a class carries several responsibilities, or fields are valid only in some situations (long method, large class, temporary field). Diagnoses and picks the treatment; mechanics are in composing-methods and moving-features.

entries.name: smell-to-treatment
entries.description: Turn one smell (named, or found in the diff or paths) into a diagnose, treat, verify, stop card with preferred, fallback and risky treatments.
entries.argumentHint: [smell name | paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: stop-and-defer
entries.description: Use when a refactoring is running long: another smell appears, cleanup keeps expanding, a treatment would cross API or ownership scope, or a visible smell should be left in place. Stop conditions, deliberate exceptions, deferred smells; choosing is treatment-choice.

entries.name: treatment-choice
entries.description: Use when choosing among refactoring treatments for a diagnosed smell: smallest technique first, fallbacks, risky options, and rejecting polymorphism, wrappers, parameter objects or superclasses that do not earn their cost. Stopping and deferring are stop-and-defer.

entries.name: type-codes-and-switches
entries.description: Use when a switch or repeated if chain branches on a type, mode or status, a type code controls behavior, or null checks dominate a branch. Decides among explicit methods, type class, subclasses, state or strategy, polymorphism and null object. Not local rewrites (conditional-moves).

entries.name: when-to-refactor
entries.description: Use when deciding whether to refactor now or later: third occurrence of duplication, before or after a feature, during a bug fix or review, or when debt slows the current change. Not for how to do it (refactoring-process) or how to treat duplication (change-locality).

entries.name: mode-labeled-steps
entries.description: Tags every change REFACTOR, FEATURE or BUGFIX and delivers them as separate sections in review order, so structure and behavior are never one indistinguishable edit.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the smell, treatment and stop rule behind each refactoring decision and checks understanding with one question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated refactoring steps and asks before any change larger than a few lines or touching a public interface.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers only with a ranked findings table against the Refactoring.Guru review questions; no rewrites unless asked; says No findings explicitly.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first and brief: what changed, which technique, which check ran, what was left; failing output still shown in full.

entries.name: mode-treatment-card
entries.description: Prints a smell, cost, technique, check and stop card before every edit and a one-line result after it, so no change happens without a diagnosis.

entries.name: bloat-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of oversized units. Use proactively after edits that grow a method, add responsibilities to a class, or add fields that are used by only one operation: long method, large class, temporary field.

entries.name: call-contract-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of call shape and contracts. Use proactively after edits that rename methods, add or remove parameters, split queries from modifiers, replace flags with methods, change setters, constructors or factories, or change how failure is reported.

entries.name: change-locality-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of where knowledge lives. Use proactively after edits that touch many files for one requirement, add a reason to change to an already busy class, or copy logic that exists elsewhere: shotgun surgery, divergent change, duplicate code.

entries.name: characterizer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests pinning current behavior before a risky refactoring, and never edits production code. Use when a planned move, extraction or substitution has no covering test and the user asked for a safety net first.

entries.name: comment-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of comments as a smell. Use proactively after edits that add or change comments above blocks, beside cryptic names or conditions, or that record assumptions about state: gives every comment a disposition.

entries.name: compatibility-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of changes to externally reachable surface. Use proactively after edits that delete, rename, inline, hide or retype anything exported, or change a signature, constructor, visibility or supertype: judges each against compatibility handling.

entries.name: coupling-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of who knows what about whom. Use proactively after edits that add methods reading another object's fields, long call chains, forwarding classes, data-only classes with logic in clients, or repeated workarounds for a library gap.

entries.name: data-modeling-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of data modeling choices. Use proactively after edits that add primitives with domain meaning, arrays used by position, long parameter lists, repeated parameter groups, or new value types and parameter objects.

entries.name: dead-code-remover
entries.description: Implementer that deletes or inlines unused code only after reachability evidence exists. Use when dead-weight candidates were found and checked, and the user asked for the removal; it refuses candidates without evidence.

entries.name: dead-weight-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of structure that may not earn its cost. Use proactively after edits that add parameters, hooks, interfaces, options or subclasses without a second user, or that leave unused code behind: dead code, lazy class, speculative generality.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the ten Refactoring.Guru review questions against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence. Use before declaring a refactoring done, committing, or opening a pull request.

entries.name: hierarchy-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of inheritance structure. Use proactively after edits that add or change subclasses, interfaces or superclasses, pull members up or push them down, or collapse a hierarchy: refused bequest, mirrored hierarchies, alternative classes.

entries.name: intent-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of change intent. Use proactively after edits that are described as a refactoring, cleanup or tidy-up, or when a diff mixes structural changes with new rules, changed defaults, or bug fixes. Labels each hunk and finds hidden behavior changes.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for refactoring work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review to decide, in at most five steps, which reviewers, implementers and skills apply and in what order. Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: method-body-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of rewritten method bodies. Use proactively after extractions, inlinings, temp changes, consolidated conditions, guard clauses or control-flag removal: checks what is read, written, evaluated and in what order, before and after.

entries.name: method-extractor
entries.description: Implementer that extracts one fragment at a time into a purpose-named method with full variable accounting. Use when a long method or commented block has been diagnosed and the user asked for the extraction.

entries.name: refactorer
entries.description: Implementer that carries out a list of refactoring findings, one named technique per step, with tests after each. Use when a review, audit or smell card has produced findings and the user asked for changes within a defined scope.

entries.name: responsibility-mover
entries.description: Implementer that moves members between classes: Move Method, Move Field, Extract Class, Inline Class, with temporary delegation. Use when a data-ownership or class-size finding has been confirmed and the user asked for the move.

entries.name: safety-net-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of verification evidence for refactorings. Use proactively after a refactoring that moves, extracts, inlines or restructures code, or that touches tests: it maps each risky step to the check that protects it and finds weakened or deleted tests.

entries.name: scope-guard
entries.description: Reviewer of refactoring scope. Use proactively after a refactoring or cleanup to compare the diff with the named smell and stop condition: it flags extra smells chased, mechanical treatments, speculative abstractions and untreated smells left unreported.

entries.name: type-introducer
entries.description: Implementer that introduces a value type, parameter object or object replacing an array, after its semantics are written down. Use when a data-modeling finding was confirmed and the user asked for the new type.

entries.name: type-switch-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of type-based branching. Use proactively after edits that add a case to a switch or if chain on a type, mode or status, introduce a type code, or add subclasses, state or strategy objects to replace one.

entries.name: api-contracts
entries.description: Use when designing or changing an API, event schema or integration contract: error responses, retryable versus non-retryable outcomes, call granularity, versioning, and documented timeout and retry expectations. Checking incoming data is `release-it-data-boundaries`; staged rollout is `release-it-release-risk`.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for production-survival hot spots, rate each failure domain, and return the top five with their owning skills in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: back-pressure
entries.description: Use when an endpoint, consumer or job accepts work and nothing says what happens at overload, or when adding rate limits, concurrency caps, rejection, load shedding or reserved capacity, or limiting abusive or malformed traffic. The contents and monitoring of a buffer are `release-it-queues`.

entries.name: bulkheads
entries.description: Use when workloads or dependencies share a thread pool, connection pool or worker capacity, when one slow integration could starve the rest, or when mapping single points of failure and fan-out. Partitions capacity in advance; stopping calls to a sick dependency is `release-it-circuit-breakers`.

entries.name: caching
entries.description: Use when adding or changing a cache, memoization, CDN rule or read-through store, or when a cache miss, expiry or outage would send load to the source of truth. Covers miss storms, stale data, outage behavior, dogpiles. Demand limits in general are `release-it-back-pressure`.

entries.name: call-chain-budget
entries.description: Compute worst-case time and attempt multiplication along a request path: per-layer time limits, retries and who owns them, mismatched deadlines and nested retries. Produces a table and a proposed single retry owner.
entries.argumentHint: [entry point, route or job | empty to ask]

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the Release It! final checklist against your current change, with yes, no or not-applicable and evidence for each, and a next action for every no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: circuit-breakers
entries.description: Use when a dependency can fail slowly or for long and callers keep hammering it, when adding a breaker, fast-fail path, fallback or degraded mode, or when a fallback is silent. Reacts to observed dependency health; partitioning is `release-it-bulkheads`, precondition checks are `release-it-stability-patterns`.

entries.name: data-boundaries
entries.description: Use when code accepts external input or reads a dependency's response (bodies, messages, files) and decides what to trust. Covers status, shape and plausibility checks, parse versus domain errors, validating before caching or enqueueing. Dead-lettering is `release-it-queues`; your contract is `release-it-api-contracts`.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Release It! rule: its strength (must, should, must not), the failure it prevents, how to check it, an original example and the exceptions the source gives.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | section | situation you are unsure about]

entries.name: failure-mode-scan
entries.description: Walk one flow's boundaries through the source's six stability assumptions and return a table of what happens when each is slow, down or wrong, the gaps and the owning skills, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [flow, endpoint, job or path | empty for the flows touched by the current diff]

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given Release It! findings with the smallest change per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Flags every number chosen without a source. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: game-day-plan
entries.description: Plan a chaos experiment, disaster drill or game day: hypothesis, steady-state signals, blast radius, stop condition, recovery path and feedback into design. Produces a plan for humans to run. Never injects faults.
entries.argumentHint: [system or flow and the failure to rehearse | hypothesis | empty to ask]

entries.name: incident-review
entries.description: Turn an incident, outage or capacity problem into a failure chain, missing defenses, detection gaps and ranked design changes, using only the evidence provided. Not a blame exercise.
entries.argumentHint: [incident description | path to postmortem, log or metrics export | empty to ask]

entries.name: launch-check
entries.description: Go or no-go for putting a service into production: look for evidence of rollback, startup validation, health, limits, signals, security and rehearsal, and return a verdict with the missing items in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [service directory | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: logging
entries.description: Use when adding or reviewing log statements, catch blocks, error handlers or retry loops, or when an incident left no usable trail. Covers structured context, correlation identifiers, failure logging, secrets, log spam and silent failure. Counts and timings are `release-it-metrics`.

entries.name: metrics
entries.description: Use when adding instrumentation, dashboards or alerts, or when a failure would be invisible: the minimum signal set of request rate, success and failure counts, dependency latency, timeouts, queue depth, retries, breaker state and saturation. Events with context are `release-it-logging`.

entries.name: operational-controls
entries.description: Use when adding or changing an admin endpoint, control plane, kill switch or the access, audit and stop controls of delivery tooling that can affect production, or reviewing secrets and admin access. Rerun safety is `release-it-restartable-automation`; rollout staging is `release-it-release-risk`.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a change that crosses a boundary before editing: failure semantics per boundary, limits, rollout and rollback, signals and tests. Produces a plan only; edits nothing.
entries.argumentHint: [change description | empty to plan the current diff's follow-up]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Release It! production-survival rules to services, APIs, jobs, queues, deployment paths and control tooling. Use for any task that adds or changes code crossing a process boundary, holding a scarce resource, buffering work, or shipping to production. Routes to the specialist components.

entries.name: queues
entries.description: Use when adding or reviewing a queue, buffer, channel, consumer, work list or dead-letter setup, or when producers can outpace consumers. Covers bounds, full behavior, depth and age monitoring, parking failing messages. Message validity is `release-it-data-boundaries`; entry-point overload is `release-it-back-pressure`.

entries.name: release-risk
entries.description: Use when planning how a change reaches production: rollout steps, exposure, rollback, version coexistence, config changes, or treating passing QA as proof of readiness. Resumable scripts are `release-it-restartable-automation`; pipeline access is `release-it-operational-controls`; interface shape is `release-it-api-contracts`.

entries.name: resilience-testing
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing automated tests for failure behavior: timeouts, retries and backoff, degraded dependencies, overload and queue saturation, restartable scripts, startup and health failures. Tests that prove a defense works. Experiments on a running system are `release-it-game-day-plan`.

entries.name: resource-budgets
entries.description: Use when code takes threads, database connections, sockets, file descriptors, memory or CPU worker slots, holds a lock or connection across a slow call, or loads or returns large collections. Covers budgets, release, streaming, pagination. Splitting capacity by workload is `release-it-bulkheads`.

entries.name: restartable-automation
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing deployment scripts, migrations, one-time jobs or runbooks that touch many machines or may be rerun after partial failure. Covers idempotent steps, durable checkpoints, resuming. Rollout staging is `release-it-release-risk`; who may run them is `release-it-operational-controls`.

entries.name: retries
entries.description: Use when code repeats a failed call, redelivers a message, or sits behind a client or gateway with automatic retries. Covers eligibility, bounded attempts and time, backoff with jitter, permanent failures, retries stacked across layers. Wait limits are `release-it-timeouts`; job schedules are `release-it-scheduled-work`.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Release It! rules, domain by domain, and report ranked findings with the owning skill for each.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: scheduled-work
entries.description: Use when adding or reviewing cron jobs, periodic tasks, timers, batch runs or long-running background work. Covers spreading start times, failure and retry policy, backoff, bounded runtime, progress, cancellation. Client-call retries are `release-it-retries`; job buffers are `release-it-queues`.

entries.name: stability-patterns
entries.description: Use when choosing a stability pattern by failure mode: steady state (no manual cleanup), fail fast on a request-time precondition or scarce resource, let it crash, decoupling middleware, or a governor. Startup and config checks are `release-it-startup-and-health`; breakers and bulkheads have own skills.

entries.name: startup-and-health
entries.description: Use when a process starts, reads configuration, exposes health or readiness endpoints, registers with a load balancer, or does heavy work at boot. Covers fail-fast startup, truthful health, handshaking. Rerunnable scripts are `release-it-restartable-automation`; tests of these are `release-it-resilience-testing`.

entries.name: timeouts
entries.description: Use when code makes an outbound call or waits on something outside the process (HTTP, RPC, database, queue, lock, future) and you must decide how long one attempt may take. Covers explicit limits, per-dependency budgets, deadlines. Repeating is `release-it-retries`; ceasing to call is `release-it-circuit-breakers`.

entries.name: mode-failure-first
entries.description: Before any design or edit, prints a failure ledger for each boundary the task touches (slow, down, wrong, what protects it, the gap), tags each edit with a ledger row, and lists the failure modes left open.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Release It! rule behind each production-survival decision, says how strong the rule is, and checks understanding with one question.

entries.name: mode-operator
entries.description: Ends each non-trivial change with an operations note addressed to whoever runs the system: what to watch, how to stop it, how to undo it, and what users see when it degrades.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps, asks before any change larger than a few lines, before touching a public API, and before choosing any timeout, limit or retry value.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against the Release It! rules, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly when clean.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first, no preamble, a few lines at most, still shows failing output in full and still flags numbers chosen without a source.

entries.name: automation-hardener
entries.description: Implementer that makes deployment scripts, migrations and one-time jobs restartable: already-done probes, atomic checkpoints, halt on first failure and an opt-in dry-run flag. Use when review findings call for resumable operational automation.

entries.name: cache-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of cache behavior under failure: cold starts, miss storms, stale data, cache outages, dogpiles and correctness hidden in cache freshness. Use proactively after edits that add or change a cache, memoization, TTL, read-through store or CDN rule.

entries.name: call-hardener
entries.description: Implementer that gives named outbound call sites explicit time limits, a single safe and bounded retry owner, and response checks, in small test-backed steps. Use when review findings call for timeouts, retry fixes or response validation at specific call sites.

entries.name: contract-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of API and integration contracts: declared failure modes, retryable versus non-retryable outcomes, call granularity, versioning and documented timeout and retry expectations. Use proactively after edits to endpoints, error responses, event schemas or client SDKs.

entries.name: control-plane-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of administrative controls and delivery tooling: authorization, audit, safe defaults, stop mechanisms, secrets and permissions. Use proactively after edits to admin endpoints, control planes, pipelines, kill switches, replay or purge utilities and ops scripts.

entries.name: data-boundary-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of input and response validation: status, content type, shape and plausibility checks, parse versus domain errors, and bad data reaching caches, queues or downstream systems. Use proactively after edits that parse requests, messages, files or dependency replies.

entries.name: deployment-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how a change ships: rollout stages, rollback or roll-forward, version coexistence, configuration changes, deployment scripts, migrations and one-time jobs. Use proactively after edits to deploy scripts, migrations, release tooling, runbooks or schema changes.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the Release It! final checklist against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence per item. Use before declaring work done, committing, or opening a pull request.

entries.name: hazard-scanner
entries.description: Mechanical scanner that counts hazard patterns (calls with no visible time limit, unbounded queues, swallowed errors, whole-collection loads, constant-green health, clock-boundary schedules) with file and line. Use before an audit or review to get raw candidates. It makes no judgments.

entries.name: isolation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of failure isolation: circuit breakers, fast failure, fallbacks, shared pools, fan-out and single points of failure. Use proactively after edits that add dependencies, executors, connection pools, fallbacks or per-item remote calls.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Release It! work. Use first on any non-trivial change, incident or readiness question to decide which specialists, skills and workflows apply, in what order (at most five steps). Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: observability-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of diagnosability: structured failure logs, correlation identifiers, secrets in logs, swallowed errors and the minimum metric set at each failure point. Use proactively after edits that add catch blocks, dependencies, queues, retries or breakers.

entries.name: overload-hardener
entries.description: Implementer that adds bounds and overload behavior in small, test-backed steps: queue and buffer capacities, rejection with retry hints at entry points, dead-letter handling, pool bounds and request size limits. Use when review findings call for limits, shedding or bounded queues.

entries.name: overload-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of overload handling from the door to the consumer: entry-point limits, rejection, shedding, reserved capacity, queue bounds, age monitoring and dead letters. Use proactively after edits that add endpoints, consumers, queues or batch triggers.

entries.name: resilience-test-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of failure-behavior tests: which defenses have no test proving them, and which tests would still pass if the defense were removed. Use proactively after edits that add timeouts, retries, breakers, limits, fallbacks, health checks or restartable scripts.

entries.name: resilience-test-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes tests for failure behavior: stalled peers, retry attempt bounds, degraded dependencies, queue saturation, interrupted scripts and startup failures. Writes tests only and never edits production code. Use when test gaps are reported.

entries.name: resource-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of scarce-resource budgets: threads, connections, sockets, descriptors, memory, release paths, locks held across slow calls and unbounded payloads. Use proactively after edits that acquire resources, size pools, or load or return large collections.

entries.name: retry-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of retry policy: eligibility, attempt and time bounds, backoff and jitter, permanent failures, and retries stacked across layers. Use proactively after edits that add retry loops, retry decorators, client retry settings or message redelivery.

entries.name: schedule-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of scheduled and background work: start-time concentration, failure and retry policy, backoff, overlap, maximum runtime, progress and cancellation. Use proactively after edits that add cron entries, timers, periodic tasks, batch jobs or long-running workers.

entries.name: startup-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the process lifecycle: startup validation, health and readiness meaning, handshaking, boot-time work and routing freshness. Use proactively after edits to main, bootstrap, configuration loading, health endpoints, shutdown or load balancer registration.

entries.name: timeout-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of time limits on outbound calls and waits. Use proactively after edits that add or change HTTP, RPC, database, cache or broker clients, blocking waits, pool checkouts or lock acquisition.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository against The Pragmatic Programmer, rate each concern, and return the top hot spots with their owning skills in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: automation
entries.description: Use when work depends on repeated manual steps: setup, build, test, lint, package, deploy or release rituals, README step lists, 'works on my machine' scripts, or bulk edits made by hand. Slow or flaky checks are `pragmatic-programmer-feedback-loops`; code derived from a spec is `pragmatic-programmer-generators-and-dsls`.

entries.name: broken-windows
entries.description: Use when touched code shows small decay (suppressed warnings, commented-out code, a skipped test, a 'temporary' hack) or a quick fix would add more. Decides what to fix now, contain or leave. How far to go and how to report is `pragmatic-programmer-ownership`.

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk The Pragmatic Programmer review checklist against your current change, with yes, no or not-applicable and evidence for each, and a next action for every no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: code-communication
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing names, comments, docs, commit messages, scripts, tests or PR text where intent or rationale is missing, or a comment restates the code. Covers every written artifact. Reporting to the user is `pragmatic-programmer-ownership`; assumptions enforced in code are `pragmatic-programmer-contracts`.

entries.name: contracts
entries.description: Use when a routine's assumptions live in comments or caller folklore, when adding assertions, preconditions, postconditions or invariants, or when impossible states return nonsense values. Defines the obligations; how failures travel is `pragmatic-programmer-error-recovery`; comments and names are `pragmatic-programmer-code-communication`.

entries.name: debug-session
entries.description: Walk one defect through reproduce, observe, isolate, explain, fix and verify with an evidence record. Stops at the explanation unless a fix is requested. Fixes with a regression test and never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [symptom, failing test or error text | add 'and fix' to also fix | empty to ask]

entries.name: debugging
entries.description: Use when a bug, failing test, intermittent failure or surprising behavior must be explained, or when code works for reasons nobody can explain. Covers reproduce, observe, isolate, explain, fix, verify. Failure design is `pragmatic-programmer-error-recovery`; which tests protect the fix is `pragmatic-programmer-test-portfolio`.

entries.name: dry-knowledge
entries.description: Use when the same rule, validation, status mapping, calculation or config meaning exists in more than one place (UI, API, service, database, docs, tests), or before copying logic. Picks one owner per fact. Generated code and rule languages are `pragmatic-programmer-generators-and-dsls`.

entries.name: error-recovery
entries.description: Use when writing or reviewing how failures travel: where an error is detected, what context survives, whether callers can tell retryable, recoverable and permanent failures apart, and where it stops. Expectations are `pragmatic-programmer-contracts`; cleanup is `pragmatic-programmer-resource-discipline`; a defect's cause is `pragmatic-programmer-debugging`.

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Pragmatic Programmer rule: its strength (must, should, must not), the failure it prevents, how to check it, an original example and the exceptions the source gives.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | section | situation you are unsure about]

entries.name: feedback-loops
entries.description: Use when tests or checks are slow, flaky, environment-dependent or run too late, when failures are hard to see, or before declaring work done. Covers the speed and visibility of the signal. Which tests a change needs is `pragmatic-programmer-test-portfolio`; scripting repeated manual steps is `pragmatic-programmer-automation`.

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given Pragmatic Programmer findings with the smallest change per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Flags behavior changes. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: generators-and-dsls
entries.description: Use when code is generated, scaffolded or produced by a tool or macro, when a small domain language or rules file is proposed, or when metaprogramming hides behavior. Existing copies of a rule are `pragmatic-programmer-dry-knowledge`; scripts for repeated work are `pragmatic-programmer-automation`; throwaway code is `pragmatic-programmer-prototypes`.

entries.name: knowledge-map
entries.description: Inventory the system facts in a directory or repository: every place each business rule, validation, mapping, calculation or config meaning is represented, whether the copies agree, and a proposed owner, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | named fact such as 'order cancellation' | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: manual-step-hunt
entries.description: Hunt for manual rituals: step lists in docs, local commands that differ from CI, unscripted release steps and hidden environment assumptions, with the script that would replace each, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: orthogonality
entries.description: Use when one change forces edits in many unrelated places, two modules share a responsibility, or policy, mechanism, data, presentation, orchestration and computation are tangled. Shared mutable state is `pragmatic-programmer-shared-state`; reach-through calls and call order are `pragmatic-programmer-shy-code`.

entries.name: ownership
entries.description: Use when asked whether a change is good enough or finished, when a trade-off, risk or uncertainty must be reported, when a poor result is blamed on the framework or deadline, or when a ritual has no benefit. Small decay is `pragmatic-programmer-broken-windows`; repository artifacts are `pragmatic-programmer-code-communication`.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a non-trivial change before editing: the real need, who owns each fact, the first slice, reversible versus committed choices, contracts, feedback, automation, cleanup budget and risks. Produces a plan only.
entries.argumentHint: [change description | empty to plan the follow-up to the current diff]

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies The Pragmatic Programmer rule set to everyday engineering decisions. Use for any task that writes, reviews, changes or plans code where duplicated knowledge, coupling, feedback speed, automation, contracts or ownership of the result matter. Routes to the specialist components.

entries.name: prototype-charter
entries.description: Write the charter for a prototype (question, what it proves and does not, shortcuts, isolation, stop condition, fate), or review a prototype before promotion and say what must be hardened or discarded. Plans and reports only.
entries.argumentHint: [experiment description | 'promote <path>' | empty to ask]

entries.name: prototypes
entries.description: Use when building a throwaway experiment, spike or proof of concept, or when prototype, spike or demo code is about to be reused in production. Covers what it proves, isolation, and the discard-or-harden decision. A kept thin slice is `pragmatic-programmer-tracer-bullets`; generated scaffolds are `pragmatic-programmer-generators-and-dsls`.

entries.name: requirements
entries.description: Use when a request names a solution instead of a need ('add a cache', 'use a cron job'), a spec keeps growing without removing uncertainty, or the team hesitates. Covers digging for the real requirement. Delivery order is `pragmatic-programmer-tracer-bullets`; a volatile vendor or format choice is `pragmatic-programmer-reversible-choices`.

entries.name: resource-discipline
entries.description: Use when code acquires files, connections, locks, handles, temp state or memory, or loops over data whose size can grow. Covers release on every path and in opposite order, ownership and algorithmic growth. Failure classification is `pragmatic-programmer-error-recovery`; who may mutate shared state is `pragmatic-programmer-shared-state`.

entries.name: reversible-choices
entries.description: Use when code hard-codes a vendor, database, platform, endpoint or policy that may change, or when choosing a serialization, config or file format. Covers reversibility, lock-in, plain text and versioned formats. A request that names a solution is `pragmatic-programmer-requirements`.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against The Pragmatic Programmer rules, concern by concern, and report ranked findings with the owning skill for each.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: shared-state
entries.description: Use when state is mutable and shared (globals, singletons, caches, ambient context, thread-locals), when adding threads, async tasks or locks, or a function reads hidden context. Layering is `pragmatic-programmer-orthogonality`; blackboards and call order are `pragmatic-programmer-shy-code`; releasing locks is `pragmatic-programmer-resource-discipline`.

entries.name: shy-code
entries.description: Use when code reaches through an object's internals (a.b().c().d()), needs calls in a fixed order (init before use), or a shared workspace is proposed. Covers Law of Demeter, temporal coupling and blackboards. Module-level ripple is `pragmatic-programmer-orthogonality`; mutable state is `pragmatic-programmer-shared-state`.

entries.name: test-portfolio
entries.description: Use when deciding which tests a change needs (unit, integration, error and recovery, resource exhaustion, performance), when a person found a bug and it needs a regression test, or when tests mirror internals. Speed and flakiness are `pragmatic-programmer-feedback-loops`; explaining the defect is `pragmatic-programmer-debugging`.

entries.name: tidy-touched
entries.description: Fix the cheap decay in the code a change already touches, in separate small steps with tests after each, and write containment notes for the rest. Chooses its own targets from the diff. Never widens scope; never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | empty for the files in the current diff]

entries.name: tracer-bullets
entries.description: Use when starting a new capability, sizing or sequencing work, or when many layers are being built before anything runs end to end. Covers thin end-to-end slices, small increments and honest estimates. A throwaway experiment is `pragmatic-programmer-prototypes`; the need itself is `pragmatic-programmer-requirements`.

entries.name: tracer-plan
entries.description: Define the thinnest real end-to-end slice for a new capability: what it proves, what is real and what is trivial, the one proving command, and the increments after it, ordered by risk. Produces a plan only.
entries.argumentHint: [capability to build | empty to ask]

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the Pragmatic Programmer rule behind each engineering decision, says how strong the rule is, and checks understanding with one question.

entries.name: mode-owner
entries.description: Ends each non-trivial task with an Ownership block: decisions and trade-offs, risks, what is unverified, what is reversible, and what was left alone.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps with a check after each, and asks before any change larger than a few lines, before touching a public API, and before choosing a quality bar.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table against The Pragmatic Programmer rules, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly when clean.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first, no preamble, a few lines at most, still shows failing output in full and still states a trade-off or risk when one exists.

entries.name: mode-tracer-first
entries.description: Before building a new capability, states the thinnest real end-to-end path and its proving command, builds and runs that first, then widens in steps ordered by risk.

entries.name: automation-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of repeated manual work: step lists in docs, local-versus-CI drift, unscripted release steps, hand-made bulk edits and unprotected scripts. Use proactively after edits to README steps, build files, CI definitions, scripts or release docs.

entries.name: automation-scripter
entries.description: Implementer that replaces a manual ritual with a versioned, inspectable script or build target that checks its prerequisites and defaults to safe. Use when a review or manual-step-hunt names a ritual to automate.

entries.name: bug-fixer
entries.description: Implementer that resolves one defect: reproduce with a failing test, record the explanation, make the smallest fix, verify. Use when a defect is reported or a failing test needs its cause fixed; takes a debug record if one exists.

entries.name: communication-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of written intent: names, comments, docs, commit messages, scripts and tests, and whether each carries rationale and domain meaning. Use proactively after edits that add comments, docs, scripts or tests, or when a commit message or PR text is drafted.

entries.name: contract-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of explicit contracts: preconditions, postconditions, invariants, assertions and nonsense return values, and where each is enforced. Use proactively after edits that add or change public routines, assertions, or comments describing what callers must do.

entries.name: contract-writer
entries.description: Implementer that encodes assumptions a routine already makes as checks, types and tests, without adding new business rules. Use when review findings name comment-only preconditions, scattered defensive checks or nonsense return values.

entries.name: coupling-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of coupling: what a change forces elsewhere, overlapping responsibilities, policy and presentation mixed into logic, reach-through call chains and fixed call orders. Use proactively after edits that touch several modules or add shared helpers.

entries.name: decay-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of decay in touched code: suppressed warnings, commented-out code, skipped tests, temporary hacks without an exit; classifies each as fix, contain or leave. Use proactively after edits, before declaring work done.

entries.name: failure-path-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how failures travel: detection point, context kept, retryable versus permanent classes, swallowed errors and containment boundaries. Use proactively after edits that add try/catch, error returns, wrapped errors or loops over batches.

entries.name: feedback-loop-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of the speed and visibility of feedback: slow, flaky or network-dependent checks in the fast path, late-only checks, skipped tests and opaque failures. Use proactively after edits to tests, test configuration or CI pipelines.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs The Pragmatic Programmer review checklist against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence per item. Use before declaring work done, committing, or opening a pull request.

entries.name: knowledge-consolidator
entries.description: Implementer that moves copies of one fact onto a single owner in small, test-backed steps. Use when review or a knowledge map names a duplicated rule, mapping or validation and the owner has been chosen.

entries.name: knowledge-duplication-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of duplicated knowledge: the same rule, validation, mapping, calculation or config meaning in more than one place, and whether each copy is derived, validated or independent. Use proactively after edits that add validation, status handling, calculations or constants.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Pragmatic Programmer work. Use first on any non-trivial change or review to decide which specialists, skills and workflows apply, in what order (at most five steps). Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: provenance-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of code of uncertain origin: prototype, spike, scaffold, generated and tool-derived code, and whether it was understood, hardened or silently promoted. Use proactively after edits that import experiment code or add generated files.

entries.name: resource-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of resource lifetimes and growth: acquire and release on every path, release order, ownership hand-offs and loops whose cost grows with input size. Use proactively after edits that open files, connections or locks, or loop over data that can grow.

entries.name: reversibility-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of hard-to-reverse choices: vendors, databases, platforms, policies and data formats hard-coded or unversioned, with the cost to reverse. Use proactively after edits that add an SDK, a storage format, an endpoint or a configuration scheme.

entries.name: shared-state-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of shared mutable state: globals, singletons, caches, ambient context, locks and async tasks, with owners, guards and visible assumptions. Use proactively after edits that add module-level state, threads, async code or hidden context reads.

entries.name: slice-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of delivery shape: whether a plan or change for a new capability has a real end-to-end path with a proving command, or is built layer by layer. Use proactively when a plan, design or pull request adds a capability across several layers.

entries.name: test-portfolio-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of what a change protects: a matrix of changed behaviors against the kinds of test the source names, plus regression tests for person-found bugs. Use proactively after edits that change behavior or fix a bug.

entries.name: audit
entries.description: Scan a directory or repository for legacy-change risk and return rated clusters and ranked hot spots in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: change-separation
entries.description: Use when shaping a legacy patch or reviewing its shape: keep behavior change, structural refactoring and cleanup apart, stay at the change point, take one small dependency break. Order of work is `legacy-code-legacy-loop`; whether to rewrite at all is `legacy-code-rewrite-pressure`.

entries.name: characterization-tests
entries.description: Use when current behavior is uncertain and must be captured before a change: pinning actual outputs, ugly behavior consumers rely on, suspicious results, probes. New-requirement tests are `legacy-code-focused-tests`; where to test is `legacy-code-test-points`; the order of work is `legacy-code-legacy-loop`.

entries.name: characterize
entries.description: Pin the current behavior of one function, class or branch with characterization tests, mark suspicious results, and stop at the first barrier that keeps the code from being called. Writes tests only; never changes production code.
entries.argumentHint: [function | class | file:line | behavior to pin | empty to choose from the diff]

entries.name: checklist
entries.description: Walk the nine Working Effectively with Legacy Code review questions against the current work, answering yes, no or not applicable with evidence and a next action for each no.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: construction-barriers
entries.description: Use when a class cannot be instantiated cheaply in a test: constructors that do real work, collaborators created inside methods, factory calls buried in behavior, graphs built mid-logic. Static access is `legacy-code-static-and-global`; parameters and interfaces are `legacy-code-substitution-seams`.

entries.name: effect-sketch
entries.description: Trace the effects of a change outward from its change point and return a sketch with test points, interception points and pinch points in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [function | class | file:line | planned change in a sentence]

entries.name: explain-rule
entries.description: Explain one Working Effectively with Legacy Code rule: its strength (must, should, must not), the reason, how to check it, an original example and the book's own exceptions.
entries.argumentHint: [rule name | section | situation you are unsure about]

entries.name: find-seam
entries.description: For one target and the test you want to write, name the first barrier, list candidate seams, pick the smallest, and name its technique, owning skill and implementer. Proposes only; never edits.
entries.argumentHint: [function | class | file:line] [the test you want to write, in a sentence]

entries.name: fix
entries.description: Resolve given legacy-change findings with the smallest change per finding, run the tests after each, and report. Never commits.
entries.argumentHint: [finding text | file:line | 'last review' | empty to ask]

entries.name: focused-tests
entries.description: Use when choosing test level and speed or writing tests for the requested behavior through a new seam: fast focused tests, old versus new behavior tests, real-boundary integration tests. Pinning unknown behavior is `legacy-code-characterization-tests`; finding where to look is `legacy-code-test-points`.

entries.name: hard-outputs
entries.description: Use when code writes files, calls the network, exits the process, writes the database, publishes messages or uses logging as control flow, so effects cannot be observed in a test. Clock and environment reads are `legacy-code-hidden-inputs`; decisions in handlers are `legacy-code-policy-vs-mechanism`.

entries.name: hidden-inputs
entries.description: Use when a test is not repeatable because code reads the clock, random numbers, environment variables, thread-local state or the implicit current user or request. Your own static singletons and global config are `legacy-code-static-and-global`; outgoing effects are `legacy-code-hard-outputs`.

entries.name: large-methods
entries.description: Use when changing a long method, large class or tangled branches: pure computation first, side effects second, method objects, tests around extracted parts. Adding behavior beside it is `legacy-code-sprout-and-wrap`; layers are `legacy-code-policy-vs-mechanism`; throwaway restructuring is `legacy-code-scratch-refactoring`.

entries.name: last-resort-seams
entries.description: Use only when ordinary object seams are impractical and you consider subclass-and-override, extract-and-override, link, preprocessing, import, template or text redefinition seams. Covers when they are allowed and their cleanup debt; the default choice of seam is `legacy-code-seams`.

entries.name: legacy-loop
entries.description: Use when starting a change in untested code and you need the order of work: state the delta, check protection, seam, break one dependency, change, refactor locally. Pinning is `legacy-code-characterization-tests`; patch shape is `legacy-code-change-separation`; rewrites are `legacy-code-rewrite-pressure`; routing is `legacy-code-principles`.

entries.name: plan
entries.description: Plan a change in untested code as the legacy loop: delta, protection, test points, barrier, seam, ordered steps and cleanup obligations. Plans only; never edits.
entries.argumentHint: [change request | issue text | empty to ask]

entries.name: policy-vs-mechanism
entries.description: Use when business decisions are trapped in framework entry points, UI handlers, callbacks or database-heavy code: separate policy from query, mapping and runtime, keep adapters thin. One long body is `legacy-code-large-methods`; effects behind collaborators are `legacy-code-hard-outputs`.

entries.name: principles
entries.description: Applies the Working Effectively with Legacy Code rules to changes in code that is untested, poorly understood or hard to instantiate. Use first on any such change: it states the modal convention and routes to every specialist; the order of work itself is `legacy-code-legacy-loop`.

entries.name: review
entries.description: Review a diff or paths against the Working Effectively with Legacy Code rules and report ranked findings, each with the owning skill and the implementer that can fix it. Reads only; never edits.
entries.argumentHint: [paths | git ref | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: rewrite-pressure
entries.description: Use when a rewrite, wholesale replacement, large new architecture or module-wide cleanup is proposed, or renaming and formatting are offered instead of making the change safe. Picks the next smaller verified move; work order is `legacy-code-legacy-loop`, patch shape is `legacy-code-change-separation`.

entries.name: scratch-refactoring
entries.description: Use when code is too tangled to understand before a change: throwaway restructuring, marking and grouping responsibilities, keeping exploratory edits out of the commit. Choosing what to test is `legacy-code-test-points`; a real extraction under tests is `legacy-code-large-methods`.

entries.name: seam-ledger
entries.description: Inventory existing test-only structure (override points, widened visibility, test setters, build flags, probes) and mark each keep, fold or remove, in at most 40 lines.
entries.argumentHint: [directory | glob | empty for the repository root]

entries.name: seams
entries.description: Use when deciding where a seam goes and what it is for: smallest seam, sensing versus separation, explicit over magical. Where to observe an effect is `legacy-code-test-points`; techniques live in the barrier skills and `legacy-code-substitution-seams`; subclass and build-level kinds are `legacy-code-last-resort-seams`.

entries.name: split-patch
