entries.description: Classify the hunks of a mixed legacy patch (behavior, dependency break, structure, cleanup, test) and propose an ordered split into separately verifiable steps. Proposes only; never stages or commits.
entries.argumentHint: [git ref | paths | empty for the current diff]

entries.name: sprout-and-wrap
entries.description: Use when new behavior must go into fragile code you cannot yet test: sprout method, sprout class, wrap method, wrap class, insert-beside-and-redirect. Reshaping existing code is `legacy-code-large-methods`; removing dependencies from it is the barrier skills (start at `legacy-code-seams`).

entries.name: static-and-global
entries.description: Use when static calls, singletons, global configuration or shared global state block substitution: wrappers, facades, instance delegators, getters, caller migration. Clock, randomness and environment reads are `legacy-code-hidden-inputs`; misplaced object creation is `legacy-code-construction-barriers`.

entries.name: substitution-seams
entries.description: Use when a concrete or oversized dependency blocks compiling or substituting it: narrow interfaces, adapters for framework objects, extracted implementers, parameterized methods, primitive parameters. Constructors are `legacy-code-construction-barriers`; choosing any seam is `legacy-code-seams`.

entries.name: test-points
entries.description: Use when the impact of a change is unclear and you must choose where to observe it: effect sketches, test points, interception points, pinch points. A seam's place is `legacy-code-seams`; restructuring to understand is `legacy-code-scratch-refactoring`; the pin is `legacy-code-characterization-tests`; test level is `legacy-code-focused-tests`.

entries.name: mode-characterize-first
entries.description: Before any edit to code without trustworthy tests, prints a safety preamble and writes the pin first; after the change prints a loop trace of what was pinned, seamed and left unprotected.

entries.name: mode-explorer
entries.description: Read-only understanding mode for unfamiliar legacy code: effect sketch, responsibility groups, open questions, candidate test points and seams, and one next safe move. Produces no patch.

entries.name: mode-mentor
entries.description: Teaches the legacy-code rule behind each decision, names its strength and the loop step it belongs to, and checks understanding with one question.

entries.name: mode-pair
entries.description: Works in small narrated steps through the legacy loop, runs tests after each, and asks before any change larger than a few lines or touching public API.

entries.name: mode-strict-reviewer
entries.description: Answers as a ranked findings table for legacy-change risks, never rewrites code unless asked, and says No findings explicitly when clean.

entries.name: mode-terse
entries.description: Result first, no preamble, a few lines unless asked, while still stating protection and showing failing output in full.

entries.name: boundary-wrapper
entries.description: Implementer that puts a clock, random source, environment read, file write, network call, process exit, database write or message behind a small collaborator, in tested steps. Use when hidden-input or hard-output findings call for injection.

entries.name: change-intent-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of patch shape in legacy changes: labels each hunk by intent and flags mixed behavior and structure, broad edits, rewrites as the first move, cosmetic-only refactoring and new hidden dependencies. Use proactively before committing or opening a pull request.

entries.name: characterization-writer
entries.description: Implementer that writes characterization tests for a list of named targets without asking questions, marking suspicious results instead, and never touching production code. Use when several targets need pins before a change, or when pins can be written unattended.

entries.name: collaborator-injector
entries.description: Implementer that turns a hard-coded collaborator into an explicit input: parameterize constructor or method, extract a narrow interface, adapt a parameter, expose a static method. Use when construction or substitution findings call for a seam in a class.

entries.name: construction-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of construction barriers: constructors that do real work, collaborators created inside methods, hidden factory calls and object graphs built mid-logic. Use proactively after edits to classes that a test cannot instantiate cheaply.

entries.name: final-gate
entries.description: Pre-merge gate that runs the nine Working Effectively with Legacy Code review questions against the working diff and returns PASS or FAIL with evidence. Use before declaring legacy work done, committing or opening a pull request.

entries.name: global-encapsulator
entries.description: Implementer that wraps statics, singletons and global configuration behind a narrow facade and migrates callers incrementally, testing after each batch. Use when static-and-global findings call for a wrapper and a caller migration.

entries.name: hard-output-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of hard outputs: direct file writes, network calls, process exits, database writes, message publication and logging used as control flow inside logic. Use proactively after edits to code that has effects a test cannot observe or avoid.

entries.name: hidden-input-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of hidden inputs: clock, randomness, environment variables, thread-local state and the implicit current user or request read from inside logic. Use proactively after edits to code that reads ambient values or when a test is not repeatable.

entries.name: large-method-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of edits to large methods and classes: extraction order, pure versus effect code, branches changed at once, tests around extracted parts. Use proactively after edits inside a long method or a class whose body defeats local reasoning.

entries.name: lead
entries.description: Triage lead for Working Effectively with Legacy Code work. Use first on any non-trivial change to code without trustworthy tests to decide which specialists, workflows and skills apply, in what order (at most five steps). Routes only; does not review.

entries.name: method-extractor
entries.description: Implementer that carves pure computation out of a large method or a handler holding decisions, one extraction at a time under a broad pin, then isolates effects if asked. Use when large-method or policy-mechanism findings call for an extraction.

entries.name: policy-mechanism-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of business decisions trapped in framework entry points, UI handlers, callbacks and database-heavy code, and of adapter thickness. Use proactively after edits to route handlers, listeners, controllers or functions that mix queries, mapping and rules.

entries.name: protection-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of test protection for legacy changes: whether modified logic has trustworthy tests and whether characterization tests are honest. Use proactively after edits to code that has few or no tests, or after characterization tests were added.

entries.name: seam-cleaner
entries.description: Implementer that retires or folds test-only structure once safer structure exists: probes, sensing variables, test setters, override points, widened visibility. Use when seam-ledger or legacy-code-seam-reviewer rows are marked fold or remove.

entries.name: seam-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of seams a change adds: kind, sensing or separation, size, explicit or magical, last-resort tier and cleanup path. Use proactively after edits that add parameters, interfaces, override points, test setters, build flags or probes for testability.

entries.name: sprout-opportunity-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of how new behavior enters fragile code: deep edits where a sprout or wrap would lower risk, and sprouts and wraps done badly. Use proactively after a change adds a rule, step or condition inside a long or untested function.

entries.name: sprouter
entries.description: Implementer that adds requested behavior beside fragile code as a sprouted method or class or as a wrap, with tests for the new unit and a one-call insertion point. Use when a rule, step or condition must enter a long or untested function without deep edits.

entries.name: static-global-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of static and global reach-through: static calls, singletons, global configuration and shared global state used from logic, and new reach-through the diff adds. Use proactively after edits that call a static helper, a singleton or a global setting.

entries.name: test-level-reviewer
entries.description: Reviewer of test level, speed and focus in legacy changes: tests through the seam, old versus new behavior tests, broad tests as scaffolding, integration tests at real boundaries. Use proactively after tests are added or changed around a legacy change.
